EXAMINER PRESENTATION DEFENSE FRAMEWORK

How to Answer & Rehearsal Protocol

The 4-step answer sequence, rehearsable 5-sentence templates, wording traps to avoid, and quick-jump navigation chips for likely examiner attacks.

🎯

Mandatory Answer Sequence: What it does → Why we chose it → Proof → Boundary

Whenever an examiner asks about any story, feature, or defect, follow this sequence strictly. Say This First before diving into code or edge cases:

⏱️ First 10 Seconds Protocol (Say This Exactly):

"This is [story ID / feature name]. I will show the live behaviour first, then its Jira acceptance criteria, the exact PR and commit, CI, the named EP/BVA test and execution record, and the matching slide."

Step 1
What It Does

Business outcome and primary role benefit.

Step 2
Why We Chose It

BDR customer clarification or ADR architectural rationale.

Step 3
Technical Proof

Exact PR number, migration filename, or automated test case.

Step 4
System Boundary

Where the responsibility ends or intentional limits.

5-Sentence Rehearsal Pattern:
  1. "This feature lets [role] do [business outcome]."
  2. "We chose it because [requirement/risk from BDR/ADR]."
  3. "The key trade-off was [alternative rejected]."
  4. "We prove it with [PR / commit / execution run record / test file]."
  5. "Its current boundary is [honest limitation]."
Status Legend: Done Partial Open defect Historical decision Precision: A venue block can be created over confirmed bookings without being blocked.
⚡ Top Likely Examiner Questions (Click to Jump & Filter) instant local search for this static guide
⚠️

Top 3 Examiner Traps & Exact Defense Realities

Trap 1: Double-Booking Concurrency (Rule B)

Examiner asks: "Show me where double-booking concurrency is handled in the app."

Defense: Concurrency race is E06-S06 / SCRUM-50 (NOT E06-S03 which is request creation). PR #378 (commit 3ac65827), test backend/tests/venueBooking.concurrency.test.ts, Slide 5. PostgreSQL exclusion constraint enforces first accepted claim wins; losing concurrent request returns 409 Conflict with buffered timeframe.

Trap 2: Operational Safety Review Workflow Split

Examiner asks: "Log in as Safety Officer and show E08-S03 approval."

Defense: E08-S03 is Coordinator submitting readiness into Safety Review (PR #283 / c44c6afd). Safety Officer evaluation and decision is E08-S06 (PR #392 / commit 44d08267) at /safety/queue → /safety/review/:eventId. All 7 factors need a choice and comment; approval goes directly to Confirmed (T-107).

Trap 3: Defect Audit Boundary (defects.md vs SCRUM-261 HEAD)

Examiner asks: "Why does defects.md say D-01..D-03 are Open if you claim you fixed them?"

Defense: docs/testing/defects.md was frozen at the 6 Nov morning audit boundary per team convention. The remediation was merged later that day under technical enabler SCRUM-261 (PRs #450, #453, #454). We declare this boundary with total transparency: D-01..D-03 are merged on main; D-04 remains intentionally open.

Mechanical Role Rehearsal & Verified Click Paths

Never guess or type unmapped URLs during the oral exam. Use these exact verified paths:

Role Correct Click Path Examiner Trap to Avoid
Organiser (Ji Ning) Login → Events → New request → /organiser/new-request /events/new is NOT a route. Full submit requires all 10 fields, future start, end after start. Drafts have lighter validation.
Coordinator (Amareet) Login → Review queue (/coordinator/queue) → select event → Venue search / bookings / Readiness /events is organiser event list. Venue booking work is event-scoped (/coordinator/events/:eventCode/venues), not global /venues/search. Do not hunt for "Under Review tab".
Venue Staff (Aaron) Login → Inventory → Maintenance blocks → /venue/blockout A block overlapping another unavailability is refused. A block over an existing booking flags that booking Conflicting (E05-S06).
Technical Support (Lexin) Login → Technician staffing (/support/technicians) → open support request → select colleague → confirm /support is a mock dashboard. An overlapping colleague shows a warning; demonstrate refusal after confirmation flow, not merely queue row.
Safety Officer (Bryan) Login → Safety review queue (/safety/queue) → choose event (/safety/review/:eventId) /safety is NOT a route. All 7 factors need a choice and comment; approval requires all satisfactory, request-changes requires ≥1 unsatisfactory.
Attendee (XY) Login → Discover (/attendee/discover) → choose confirmed event → Register (/attendee/register/:eventCode) or waitlist /catalog is NOT a route. Closed or unconfirmed registration cannot proceed. Full event offers waitlist.

Examiner Wording Traps & Exact System Realities

  • Obsolete Change Requests: When an event completes or is cancelled, the lifecycle service atomically marks its pending change requests Obsolete in the same transaction. (Never claim it is triggered asynchronously by a background scheduler).
  • Workbook Case Count: Exactly 391 functional story cases + 3 cross-cutting DoD/performance cases = 394 workbook cases across 65 user stories.
  • Defect Integrity Rule: Admit honestly · do not count as Done. Never claim open defects pass DoD.

Act 6: CI Pipeline & Guardrails
Template Question

What are the most interesting things in your CI Pipeline that you wish to highlight? Why? Where did you get the idea from, and what benefits do you get from this?

Slide Bullet Content (PPTX)
1. **Backlog to test drift check:** `scripts/tc_coverage_audit.py` and `scripts/check_test_case_references.py` fail the build if a test case cites a scenario that no longer exists or was superseded 2. **Merge queue:** checks re-run on top of the latest `main` plus every PR ahead in the queue, so you don't need to "update branch" and get re-approved 3. **Diagrams render in CI:** the C4 Mermaid file must render (`mmdc`), so a broken architecture diagram fails the build (it caught one on `main` on 30 Oct) 4. **Evidence hygiene:** a run record and its screenshots must land in the same commit; secrets are scanned (detect-secrets, TruffleHog) - Where the ideas came from: our own Sprint 2 retro (merge conflicts, stale approvals), Week 6 and 9 lectures (CI, regression), and GitHub's merge queue docs - Benefit: docs and tests can't silently drift from the backlog, and reviewers stopped re-approving the same PR

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Valid credentials accepted

Given I am a registered user with valid credentials When I submit my email address and password Then I am signed in and taken to the dashboard for my role

Scenario 2 — Wrong password reveals nothing

Given I am a registered user When I submit an incorrect password Then I remain signed out and see a message that does not reveal whether the email address is registered

Scenario 3 — Lockout on fifth failure

Given I have submitted 5 consecutive incorrect passwords When I attempt to sign in again Then my account is locked and I am shown how to reset my password

Scenario 4 — Reset link issued

Given my account is locked When I request a password reset Then a reset link is sent to my registered email address

Scenario 5 — Lock lifted on new password

Given I have followed a valid reset link When I set a new password Then the lock is lifted and I can sign in with the new password

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Sign in with a valid email and password and reach the dashboard for my role
  • ☑ Be refused on an incorrect password without learning whether the email is registered
  • ☑ Be locked out on the 5th consecutive failed attempt
  • ☑ Receive a reset link at my registered email address
  • ☑ Regain access once the password has been reset
  • ☑ Have the lockout recorded in the activity log (E14-S02)

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Own client's events only

Given I am signed in as an Event Organiser for Client A When I open my event list Then only events belonging to Client A are shown

Scenario 2 — Direct access refused

Given an event belongs to a client organisation I am not linked to When I navigate directly to that event's identifier Then access is refused and the attempt is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 3 — Colleague's event visible

Given my organisation has several Event Organisers When a colleague from my organisation creates an event Then I can see that event in my organisation's list

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ View only events linked to their own client organisation in their event list
  • ☑ Be denied access when attempting to open (e.g. via URL or ID) an event belonging to another client organisation
  • ☑ View events created by any Organiser within their own client organisation
  • ☑ Search for events without unrelated client organisations' events appearing in the results
  • ☑ Receive notifications that never reference events belonging to unrelated client organisations
  • ☑ Confirm that a denied access attempt is captured in the activity log with the user, event and time

  • ☑ Not see events or events I am not registered for

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Valid changes saved

Given I am signed in When I save valid changes to my profile Then the updated details are stored and shown when I next open my profile

Scenario 2 — Malformed email rejected

Given I enter an email address in an invalid format When I try to save Then the change is rejected and the invalid field is identified

Scenario 3 — Duplicate email rejected

Given I enter an email address already registered to another account When I try to save Then the change is rejected

Scenario 4 — Notifications follow the new address

Given I change my email address When the change is saved Then future notifications for my events are sent to the new address

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Update name, email and contact number and see them persist
  • ☑ Be blocked from saving a malformed email address, with the field identified
  • ☑ Be blocked from taking an email address already in use
  • ☑ Receive subsequent notifications at the updated address
  • ☑ Not be able to change my own role from this screen
  • ☑ See my organisation displayed read-only, with a hint to contact my Coordinator for organisation changes (T-61)

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Account created

Given I do not have an account When I submit the required details Then an Attendee account is created and I can sign in with it

Scenario 2 — Email already in use

Given an account already exists with that email address When I submit the form Then I am told the address is already in use and no second account is created

Scenario 3 — Invalid submission corrected

Given required fields are missing or the password does not meet the stated policy When I submit Then the account is not created and I am shown what to correct

Scenario 4 — Attendee role only

Given I sign up through the public form When my account is created Then it holds the Attendee role only

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Create an Attendee account with the required details and sign in with it
  • ☑ Be told the address is already in use when an account exists, with no second account created
  • ☑ Be shown what to correct when fields are missing or the password fails the policy
  • ☑ Receive only the Attendee role from the public sign-up form
  • ☑ Not be offered any internal role during sign-up

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Deactivated and signed out

Given I am signed in When I confirm deactivation Then I am signed out and can no longer sign in with those credentials

Scenario 2 — Historical records retained

Given I have deactivated my account When ConnectSphere views an event I was linked to Then my past registrations and event records remain intact and attributed

Scenario 3 — Upcoming registration released

Given I am an Attendee registered for an upcoming event (an event whose start timestamp is in the future) When I deactivate Then my registration is withdrawn and the place is released, and this applies to both `registered` and `waitlisted` entries, and deactivation overrides the E09-S05 `withdrawal_deadline` (see T-53, T-54, T-55)

Scenario 4 — Coordinator with events blocked

Given I am an Event Coordinator with events assigned to me in an active-lifecycle status (Submitted, Under review, Clarification requested, Approved, Planning, or Confirmed) When I attempt to deactivate Then deactivation is blocked until those events are reassigned, while events in Completed, Cancelled, or Rejected status do not block deactivation (see T-52)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Deactivate my own account and be signed out immediately
  • ☑ Be unable to sign in afterwards
  • ☑ Have my historical event and registration records retained and still attributed
  • ☑ Have upcoming registrations (event start in the future) released on deactivation, including waitlisted entries, overriding the E09-S05 withdrawal deadline (Attendees; T-53, T-54, T-55)
  • ☑ Be blocked from deactivating while I hold any event in an active-lifecycle status (Submitted through Confirmed); events in Completed, Cancelled, or Rejected do not block (Coordinators; T-52)
  • ☑ Have the deactivation recorded in the activity log with actor and time

Manage only the events assigned to me as an Event Coordinator

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Coordinators only see events explicitly assigned to them, preventing accidental cross-coordinator interference in planning workspaces."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Lead Coordinators have a separate oversight route; standard Coordinators receive 403 on unassigned events.
BDR Lineage:
C-69 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur. C-40 Event Coordinators can see all events and search/view venue availability calendars; Venue Staff also access and maintain this data. T-70 Retire T-14 and rewrite E03-S01 around an unassigned queue worked by the Event Coordinator Lead T-73 Write the Week 7 stories now against recorded defaults and amend after the customer Q&A, rather than waiting T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied O-38
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-007 One single-page application for all roles (five, now seven) ADR-008 Client organisation as the tenancy boundary ADR-015 Cookie sessions everywhere; no Supabase Auth in Release 1 ADR-016 Thirty-minute login lockout after five failures

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Own assigned events only

Given events are assigned to me and to other Coordinators When I open my event list Then only the events assigned to me are shown

Scenario 2 — Direct access to a colleague's event refused

Given an event is assigned to another Coordinator When I navigate directly to its identifier or attempt any action on it Then access is refused, nothing about the event is revealed, and the attempt is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 3 — Unassigned requests not visible to Coordinators

Given requests are in the unassigned queue When I open my event list Then they are not shown, because the queue belongs to the Lead (assumes O-38)

Scenario 4 — Venue calendars still visible

Given other Coordinators' events hold venue bookings When I open a venue availability calendar Then the Free, Tentative, Confirmed and Blocked states are shown for every period while the other events' details are withheld, exactly as in E05-S03 Scenario 2

Scenario 5 — Organiser isolation unchanged

Given an Event Organiser for Client A is signed in When they open their event list Then E01-S02 Scenarios 1 to 3 hold unchanged

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ See only the events assigned to me in my event list
  • ☑ Be refused, with the attempt logged, when opening or acting on another Coordinator's event
  • ☑ Not see the unassigned queue
  • ☑ Still see every venue's availability states with other events' details withheld
  • ☑ Confirm the Organiser's client isolation (E01-S02) is unchanged

Sign in as an Event Coordinator Lead or Safety Officer

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Authentication router directs Event Coordinator Lead and Safety Officer to dedicated workspaces upon sign-in based on user_roles membership."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Lead and Safety Officer accounts are seeded with distinct credentials; multi-role switching occurs via explicit role selection.
BDR Lineage:
C-69 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur. C-70 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request). C-57 System account registration/onboarding is not in scope for Release 1. You can populate your own database with Internal staff accounts as pre-loaded/pre-created with appropriate roles and access controls for development purpose. T-72 Extend the role model from five roles to seven T-73 Write the Week 7 stories now against recorded defaults and amend after the customer Q&A, rather than waiting T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied O-44
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-007 One single-page application for all roles (five, now seven) ADR-008 Client organisation as the tenancy boundary ADR-015 Cookie sessions everywhere; no Supabase Auth in Release 1 ADR-016 Thirty-minute login lockout after five failures

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Complete request submitted

Given I am signed in as an Event Organiser and every mandatory field is complete When I submit the request Then its status becomes Submitted and I receive confirmation

Scenario 2 — Missing mandatory fields blocked

Given one or more mandatory fields are empty When I try to submit Then submission is blocked and every missing field is identified

Scenario 3 — Past date blocked

Given I enter a preferred date in the past When I try to submit Then submission is blocked with an explanation

Scenario 4 — None required satisfies a field

Given my event needs no equipment When I select 'none required' for that field Then the field counts as complete and submission proceeds

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Enter all ten mandatory fields: event name, description, purpose, preferred dates and times, expected attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, equipment requirements, layout preference, registration setup
  • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while any mandatory field is empty, with each missing field named
  • ☑ Select 'none required' for equipment, layout or registration setup where the event does not need them
  • ☑ Be blocked from submitting a preferred date in the past
  • ☑ See the status change to Submitted and receive confirmation

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Draft saved and hidden from Coordinators

Given I have partially completed a request When I save it as a draft Then it is stored with status Draft and is not visible to Event Coordinators

Scenario 2 — Draft reopened with values restored

Given I have a saved draft When I reopen it Then all previously entered values are restored

Scenario 3 — Draft deleted

Given I have a draft I no longer need When I delete it Then it is removed from my list and is not counted as an active request

Scenario 4 — Completed draft submitted

Given a draft has every mandatory field complete When I submit it Then it follows E02-S01 and its status becomes Submitted

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Save an event request without completing all mandatory fields
  • ☑ View all of my saved drafts, distinguishable from submitted requests
  • ☑ Reopen a draft and see previously entered values pre-filled
  • ☑ Continue editing a saved draft
  • ☑ Delete a draft I no longer need
  • ☑ Confirm that Event Coordinators cannot see my drafts

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Previous event copied

Given I choose one of my own completed or past events When I copy it Then ConnectSphere creates a new draft with the event requirements and Session structure copied, all event and Session dates/times left blank, and no bookings, reservations, or registrations carried over (T-99)

Scenario 2 — Missing reference flagged

Given the copied event references a venue or equipment item that no longer exists When the draft is created Then the affected requirement is flagged for review and identifies its Session rather than being copied silently

Scenario 3 — Dates remain subject to current submission policy

Given I later submit the copied draft When I enter event and Session dates Then the current E02-S01 and E02-S07 validation applies; copying does not bypass the two-year horizon or the Coordinator feasibility review

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Copy one of my own completed or past events into a new draft
  • ☑ Confirm requirements and Session structure are copied while event and Session dates/times are blank
  • ☑ Confirm bookings, equipment reservations and registrations are not copied (T-99)
  • ☑ See unavailable venue/equipment references flagged against the relevant Session
  • ☑ Submit a copied draft subject to the current date rules

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — No fixed minimum lead time

Given a requested event date is not in the past and is within the permitted horizon When I submit the request Then ConnectSphere does not reject it solely because it is fewer than a fixed number of days or months away; the assigned Coordinator assesses feasibility

Scenario 2 — Dates beyond two years rejected

Given any requested event or Session date is later than two calendar years after the Singapore-local submission date When I submit the request Then submission is blocked and the out-of-range date is identified

Scenario 3 — Two-year boundary accepted

Given every requested event and Session date is on or before the date two calendar years after the Singapore-local submission date When I submit an otherwise valid request Then the date-horizon check passes

Scenario 4 — Past Event date rule preserved

Given the requested Event date is in the past When I submit the request Then E02-S01 past-date validation still blocks it

Scenario 5 — Past Session date rejected

Given any requested Session date is in the past When I submit the request Then submission is blocked and the past Session date is identified

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit a feasible request without an invented minimum lead time
  • ☑ Be blocked when any Event or Session date exceeds two calendar years from submission
  • ☑ Pass the exact two-year boundary
  • ☑ Confirm a past Event date remains blocked by E02-S01
  • ☑ Be blocked when any Session date is in the past

E03-S01 SCRUM-32 Sprint 2 3 pts Aaron Koh ✅ Done

Assign an Event Coordinator to a request

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"On submission, system assigns the coordinator with the lowest active event workload (T-14); superseded by Lead Queue in C-69."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Done story that stays Done per T-74; Lead Queue replacement is tracked under E03-S08 and defect D-01.
BDR Lineage:
C-12 The system will assigns one Event Coordinator to an event C-41 Assignments are auto-assigned by the system (no more than 1 coordinator per event). C-55 Event co-ordinators are auto-assigned by the system and only 1 co-ordinator can be assigned to a specific event. Detail implementation is up to the team as long as it is fair and technically possible as long as it fits the requirement earlier. C-56 Reassignment should be discussed offline. Once there is an agreement, the original co-ordinator can make the change and request the new co-ordinator to accept the change. Detail process and UI implementation is up to the team. T-14 Auto-assign to the Coordinator with the fewest active events T-15 Only the currently assigned Coordinator may reassign C-69 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur. T-70 Retire T-14 and rewrite E03-S01 around an unassigned queue worked by the Event Coordinator Lead T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-007 One single-page application for all roles (five, now seven) ADR-019 Allow multiple roles per account

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — [Superseded by E03-S08 (C-69)] Exactly one Coordinator assigned

Given a request is submitted When submission completes Then the system assigns exactly one Event Coordinator, the status becomes Under Review, and that Coordinator is notified

Scenario 2 — [Superseded by E03-S08 (C-69)] Fewest active events wins

Given several Event Coordinators are available When the system assigns one Then it selects the Coordinator with the fewest active events

Scenario 3 — Reassignment requested

Given I am the assigned Coordinator and a reassignment has been agreed offline When I request reassignment to a named colleague Then the request is recorded, that colleague is notified, and I remain assigned until they accept

Scenario 4 — Reassignment accepted

Given a reassignment request is awaiting my acceptance When I accept it Then I become the assigned Coordinator, the previous assignment ends, and the change is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 5 — Reassignment declined

Given a reassignment request is awaiting acceptance When the named colleague declines it Then the original Coordinator remains assigned and is notified of the refusal

Scenario 6 — Unassigned Coordinator refused

Given I am not the assigned Coordinator When I attempt to reassign the event Then the action is refused

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm that exactly one Event Coordinator is assigned on submission (superseded by E03-S08, C-69)
  • ☑ Confirm the assigned Coordinator is the one with the fewest active events (superseded by E03-S08, C-69; the count is now shown to the Lead as advice)
  • ☑ Confirm the status moves from Submitted to Under Review
  • ☑ Request reassignment to a named colleague as the assigned Coordinator
  • ☑ Confirm the original Coordinator stays assigned until the colleague accepts
  • ☑ Accept a reassignment request and take ownership of the event
  • ☑ Decline a reassignment request, leaving the original Coordinator assigned
  • ☑ Be refused when attempting to reassign an event assigned to someone else

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Questions sent, status changes

Given I am reviewing a request with status Under Review When I record my questions and send them Then the status becomes Awaiting Clarification and the Event Organiser is notified with the questions

Scenario 2 — Organiser responds, review resumes

Given a request is Awaiting Clarification When the Event Organiser responds and resubmits Then the status returns to Under Review and I am notified

Scenario 3 — Outstanding questions visible

Given a request is Awaiting Clarification When I view it Then the outstanding questions and the date they were raised are shown

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Record one or more questions against a request under review
  • ☑ Confirm the status becomes Awaiting Clarification and the Organiser is notified
  • ☑ See the outstanding questions and the date raised on the event record
  • ☑ Confirm the status returns to Under Review when the Organiser responds
  • ☑ Filter my events by clarification status

E03-S03 SCRUM-34 Sprint 2 3 pts Aaron Koh ✅ Done

Decide on an event request

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Coordinator approves or rejects a request; approval transitions status to Approved (ready for venue planning), rejection records mandatory reasons."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Rejected events are terminal unless an administrative appeal is handled offline.
BDR Lineage:
C-09 While rejected/returned requests must retain an appropriate record of the decision, mandatory rejection reasoning fields are left to implementation design and can only be confirmed when the requirement are finalised. T-39 A rejection reason is mandatory T-41 Rejected is terminal T-43 Merge approve and reject into one E03-S03 O-06
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-007 One single-page application for all roles (five, now seven) ADR-019 Allow multiple roles per account

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Approved to planning

Given a request has status Under Review and the required information is complete When I approve it Then the status becomes Approved and the Event Organiser is notified

Scenario 2 — Incomplete request blocked

Given required information is still incomplete When I try to approve the request Then approval is blocked and the missing items are listed

Scenario 3 — Rejected with reason

Given a request is under review When I reject it and record a reason Then the status becomes Rejected, the reason is stored and the Event Organiser is notified

Scenario 4 — Rejection without reason blocked

Given I attempt to reject without recording a reason When I confirm Then the rejection is blocked

Scenario 5 — Rejected record is read-only

Given a request has been rejected When the Event Organiser views it Then the reason and the date of the decision are shown and the request is read-only

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Approve a request whose required information is complete
  • ☑ Confirm an approval sets the status to Approved and notifies the Organiser
  • ☑ Be blocked from approving an incomplete request, with the missing items listed
  • ☑ Reject a request under review with a recorded reason
  • ☑ Be blocked from rejecting without a recorded reason
  • ☑ Confirm a rejection sets the status to Rejected and notifies the Organiser
  • ☑ See the reason and decision date in plain language as the Organiser
  • ☑ Confirm a rejected request is read-only

Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/eventLifecycle/decision.ts
Database Migration: 0001_connectsphere_schema.sql
Frontend Component: frontend/src/features/coordinator/DecisionPanel.tsx

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Organiser edits before approval

Given an event has not yet been approved When the Event Organiser edits any field Then the change is saved directly against the event

Scenario 2 — Coordinator edits after approval

Given an event has been approved When I edit any field as the assigned Coordinator Then the change is saved and recorded in the activity log

Scenario 3 — Organiser edits unrestricted fields

Given an event has been approved When the Event Organiser edits the event name, description, purpose or registration dates Then the change is saved directly

Scenario 4 — Restricted edit routed to change request

Given an event has been approved When the Event Organiser attempts to change the date, time, expected attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, equipment requirements or layout Then direct editing is refused and they are directed to raise a change request (E10-S01)

Scenario 5 — Unassigned Coordinator refused

Given I am not the assigned Coordinator When I attempt to edit an approved event Then the action is refused

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Edit any field as the Organiser while the event is Draft, Submitted, Under Review or Awaiting Clarification
  • ☑ Edit any field as the assigned Coordinator once the event is Approved or later
  • ☑ Edit name, description, purpose and registration dates as the Organiser after approval
  • ☑ Be refused as the Organiser when directly editing date, time, attendance, venue requirements, accessibility needs, equipment requirements or layout after approval
  • ☑ Be redirected to the change request flow (E10-S01) when a restricted edit is attempted
  • ☑ Confirm every post-approval edit is recorded in the activity log

E03-S08 SCRUM-153 Sprint 3 5 pts Bryan Seah (Product Owner) 🚨 Open Defect (D-01 · Shipped on main) Shipped via SCRUM-261

Assign a queued request to an Event Coordinator as the Lead

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Unassigned request queue for Event Coordinator Lead to assign submissions directly per C-69/T-83; logged as D-01 in morning audit and safely shipped to main via SCRUM-261 (PR #450, #453)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Historical defect D-01: Auto-assign algorithm was active during morning audit; evening PR #450 & #453 (SCRUM-261) removed auto-assign and restored Lead queue with assigned_by tracking. 31 passing tests.
BDR Lineage:
C-69 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur. C-85 The Event Coordinator Lead manually assigns or reassigns any event to any suitable Event Coordinator. There are no restriction for this release. C-93 It is entirely at the Event Coordinator Lead's discretion based on workload, availability, or expertise; the system does not enforce automated assignment rules. C-100 The system supports multiple Event Coordinator Leads, all of whom can view the unassigned queue and all active assignments. C-105 Assignment is handled manually by the Lead from the unassigned queue. Coordinators only manage events assigned to them by the Lead. At the moment, the lead is not able to coordinate event. C-106 Leads view all unassigned/assigned event requests and active assignments system-wide. The Safety Officer views relevant event, venue, capacity, layout, and equipment details to perform safety checks. C-127 The system supports multiple Leads who can see all unassigned requests and active coordinator assignments done by him C-130 Newly submitted events enter an unassigned queue visible to Event Coordinator Leads for allocation. T-70 Retire T-14 and rewrite E03-S01 around an unassigned queue worked by the Event Coordinator Lead T-72 Extend the role model from five roles to seven T-73 Write the Week 7 stories now against recorded defaults and amend after the customer Q&A, rather than waiting T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-007 One single-page application for all roles (five, now seven) ADR-019 Allow multiple roles per account

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Submission enters the unassigned queue

Given an Event Organiser submits a request When submission completes Then no Event Coordinator is assigned, the event's status stays Submitted, the request appears in the unassigned queue, and every active Event Coordinator Lead is notified (replaces E03-S01 Scenarios 1 and 2)

Scenario 2 — Queue shows basic event information, oldest first

Given requests are in the unassigned queue When I open it as an Event Coordinator Lead Then each shows the event name, the Organiser's client organisation, preferred dates, expected attendance and the time submitted, oldest first; every Lead sees the same organisation-wide queue, and no non-Lead can view it

Scenario 3 — Lead assigns a Coordinator

Given a request is in the queue When I, as an Event Coordinator Lead, choose an Event Coordinator and assign them Then exactly one Coordinator is assigned immediately, the status becomes Under Review, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified, the request leaves the queue, and the activity log records the Lead actor and time

Scenario 4 — Workload shown while choosing

Given I am choosing a Coordinator When the list of Coordinators is shown Then each shows their count of active events, so the fewest-active-events rule the system used to apply (T-14) is available as advice without being enforced

Scenario 5 — Only a Lead may assign from the queue

Given I am not an Event Coordinator Lead When I attempt to view or assign a queued request Then the action is refused and the refusal is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 6 — Status transition and Organiser view unchanged

Given a request has been assigned from the queue When the Organiser tracks the event (E03-S05) Then the status history shows Submitted followed by Under Review exactly as it did under automatic assignment, so E03-S01's delivered transition still holds

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm a newly submitted request has no Coordinator, stays Submitted and appears in the unassigned queue
  • ☑ Confirm every active Lead is notified of each new queued request
  • ☑ See the same global queued requests and basic information, oldest first, as any Lead only
  • ☑ Assign exactly one Coordinator from the queue, moving the event to Under Review with the Coordinator and Organiser notified and the action logged
  • ☑ See each Coordinator's active-event count while choosing
  • ☑ Be refused as a non-Lead when attempting to view or assign from the queue
  • ☑ Confirm the Submitted to Under Review transition recorded by E03-S01 is unchanged

BDR Lineage:
C-69 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur. C-85 The Event Coordinator Lead manually assigns or reassigns any event to any suitable Event Coordinator. There are no restriction for this release. C-90 The Event Coordinator Lead can assign or reassign events whenever staff availability or responsibilities change, even after venue and technical arrangements are confirmed. C-93 It is entirely at the Event Coordinator Lead's discretion based on workload, availability, or expertise; the system does not enforce automated assignment rules. C-100 The system supports multiple Event Coordinator Leads, all of whom can view the unassigned queue and all active assignments. C-104 Reassignment by the Lead is direct and immediate; no formal acceptance step by the incoming Coordinator is required in the system. C-105 Assignment is handled manually by the Lead from the unassigned queue. Coordinators only manage events assigned to them by the Lead. At the moment, the lead is not able to coordinate event. C-106 Leads view all unassigned/assigned event requests and active assignments system-wide. The Safety Officer views relevant event, venue, capacity, layout, and equipment details to perform safety checks. C-127 The system supports multiple Leads who can see all unassigned requests and active coordinator assignments done by him C-128 Assignment and reassignment by the Lead take effect immediately in the system with notifications sent to relevant users. C-129 All coordinator assignments and reassignments are managed by the Event Coordinator Lead, the system do not manage the reassignment request T-70 Retire T-14 and rewrite E03-S01 around an unassigned queue worked by the Event Coordinator Lead T-73 Write the Week 7 stories now against recorded defaults and amend after the customer Q&A, rather than waiting T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Lead reassignment takes effect immediately

Given an event is assigned to a Coordinator When I, as an Event Coordinator Lead, reassign it to another Coordinator Then the change takes effect at once without an acceptance step, the outgoing and incoming Coordinators and the Organiser are notified, and the activity log records the Lead actor and time

Scenario 2 — Lead may reassign at any stage with an assignment

Given an event has an assigned Coordinator at any workflow stage When I, as an Event Coordinator Lead, select another eligible Coordinator Then the reassignment is immediate, all relevant users are notified, and the activity log preserves both the prior and new assignment

Scenario 3 — Coordinator-initiated reassignment workflow is unavailable

Given I am an assigned or unassigned Event Coordinator When I attempt to create, accept, decline or request a reassignment through the system Then the action is refused because only an Event Coordinator Lead may assign or reassign

Scenario 4 — Only a Lead may reassign

Given I am not an Event Coordinator Lead When I attempt to reassign an event Then the action is refused and recorded in the activity log

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (3 criteria)

  • ☑ Reassign an event directly as the Lead, at any assigned workflow stage, with both Coordinators and the Organiser notified and the change logged
  • ☑ Be refused when attempting to create, accept, decline or request a Coordinator-initiated reassignment
  • ☑ Be refused as any non-Lead when attempting to reassign an event

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Every active event and its Coordinator listed

Given events exist in every status When I open the oversight view Then every event whose status is Submitted, Under Review, Awaiting Clarification, Approved, Planning, Safety Review or Confirmed is listed with its assigned Coordinator or "Unassigned", and I can filter by Coordinator and by status

Scenario 2 — Workload per Coordinator

Given Coordinators have events assigned When I open the workload summary Then each Coordinator is shown with their count of active events and the list of those events

Scenario 3 — One Lead sees everything

Given multiple Event Coordinator Leads exist When any Lead opens the oversight view Then every unassigned request and active Coordinator assignment is included regardless of which Lead or Coordinator is viewing it; Lead access is organisation-wide rather than partitioned

Scenario 4 — Coordinators cannot open the oversight view

Given I am not an Event Coordinator Lead When I navigate to the oversight view Then access is refused and the attempt is recorded in the activity log

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (4 criteria)

  • ☑ See every active event with its assigned Coordinator or Unassigned, filterable by Coordinator and status
  • ☑ See each Coordinator's active-event count and events
  • ☑ Confirm every Lead sees the same organisation-wide assignments and queue, not a subset
  • ☑ Be refused as a non-Lead

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Organiser edits registration setup before approval

Given my event has not yet been approved When I edit its registration setup Then the change is saved against the event and recorded in the activity log

Scenario 2 — Registration setup cannot be cleared

Given my event has a registration setup When I try to save it empty Then the save is blocked and the recorded registration setup is unchanged

Scenario 3 — Registration setup restricted for the Organiser after approval

Given my event has been approved When I open its edit form Then the registration setup is read-only and I am directed to raise a change request (E10-S01)

Scenario 4 — Coordinator edits registration setup after approval

Given an event has been approved When I edit its registration setup as the assigned Coordinator Then the change is saved and recorded in the activity log

Scenario 5 — Registration dates laid out clearly

Given I am editing an event When I view the Registration section Then "Registration opens" and "Registration closes" are shown as two separate labelled fields, each label with its own input, with no sideways scrolling at phone width

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Edit the registration setup as the Organiser before approval, with the edit recorded in the activity log
  • ☑ Be blocked when saving an empty registration setup
  • ☑ See the registration setup read-only after approval, with a link to request a change
  • ☑ Edit the registration setup as the assigned Coordinator after approval, with the edit recorded in the activity log
  • ☑ See "Registration opens" and "Registration closes" as two labelled fields at desktop and phone width

TC_E03S12_01 — Organiser sees the shared success Alert after an allowed edit
Happy Path Acceptance (IS212 Step 2)

Scenario: Organiser sees the shared success Alert after an allowed edit

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Verifies core functional acceptance for E03-S12 - Scenario 1: proves the primary business workflow succeeds and satisfies the stakeholder specification under valid conditions.

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

Coordinator assignment transactional logic, Coordinator Lead authorization check, or event_assignments database foreign keys.

Pre-conditions: Planned, not executed. An Organiser can edit a Submitted event in a disposable local test environment; the assigned Coordinator's existing success feedback is available for comparison.

Steps: 1. Sign in as the event's Organiser and open Edit event. 2. Change the event title and save successfully. 3. Inspect the confirmation and its accessibility semantics. 4. Compare its feedback component with the Coordinator's existing save confirmation.

Expected outcome: The existing field-specific saved text names the changed title and activity log. It is rendered by shared Alert tone="success" with role="status", matching the shared success pattern rather than plain text. This case is a planned definition, not a PASS record.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

TC_E03S12_02 — Saved edit persists and its audit entry is not duplicated by feedback
Cross-Cutting Quality & Security (IS212 Step 3)

Scenario: Saved edit persists and its audit entry is not duplicated by feedback

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Enforces non-functional system invariants across module boundaries (E03-S12 - Scenario 2), ensuring single-role security isolation (ADR-012), immutable audit trail recording, or transactional notification consistency.

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

Coordinator assignment transactional logic, Coordinator Lead authorization check, or event_assignments database foreign keys.

Pre-conditions: Planned, not executed. An editable event and a tester with read-only inspection of its audit rows in a disposable local database are available; record the starting value and row count.

Steps: 1. As the Organiser, change only the event title and save. 2. Wait for the normal reload, then explicitly reload and reopen the event. 3. Inspect the saved title and corresponding activity entry. 4. Compare the audit row count and values with the single successful edit.

Expected outcome: The saved value survives reload and its existing audit entry identifies the edit. Rendering or reloading the success confirmation causes no second write or duplicate audit entry.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

TC_E03S12_03 — Invalid input retains validation feedback without success
Negative Guardrail / Business Rule (IS212 Step 4)

Scenario: Invalid input retains validation feedback without success

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Validates defensive exception handling and business rule enforcement. As emphasized in IS212 Week 4 Slide 26 and Week 6, this test proves the system rejects invalid inputs or unauthorized operations with predictable error responses (HTTP 4xx), protecting database consistency (E03-S12 - Scenario 3).

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

Coordinator assignment transactional logic, Coordinator Lead authorization check, or event_assignments database foreign keys.

Pre-conditions: Planned, not executed. The Organiser can edit a Submitted event with a nonempty title; note the stored value and audit rows.

Steps: 1. Open Edit event and clear the required title. 2. Attempt to save and inspect the form's feedback. 3. Cancel, reload and compare the stored title and audit rows.

Expected outcome: Existing field validation and error feedback remain; no success Alert claims the invalid attempt was saved. The stored title and audit rows are unchanged by the rejected attempt.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

TC_E03S12_04 — Failed request after a prior success cannot leave a false confirmation
Negative Guardrail / Business Rule (IS212 Step 4)

Scenario: Failed request after a prior success cannot leave a false confirmation

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Validates defensive exception handling and business rule enforcement. As emphasized in IS212 Week 4 Slide 26 and Week 6, this test proves the system rejects invalid inputs or unauthorized operations with predictable error responses (HTTP 4xx), protecting database consistency (E03-S12 - Scenario 3).

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

Coordinator assignment transactional logic, Coordinator Lead authorization check, or event_assignments database foreign keys.

Pre-conditions: Planned, not executed. A permitted Organiser edit has just succeeded; the local test harness can make only the next save request fail without committing it.

Steps: 1. Open a new edit after the successful save and confirm the old confirmation clears. 2. Change the title again and simulate a failed save response in the local harness. 3. Inspect the error feedback and absence of a success claim. 4. Restore the connection, cancel and reload the record; inspect audit rows.

Expected outcome: The failure uses existing error feedback, never a success Alert for the failed attempt or a stale prior success. Reload retains First change and no audit entry is added for Failed second change.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Shared success Alert after a saved edit

Given I may edit an event When a changed field saves successfully Then the event detail shows the existing field-specific saved message through the shared Alert with tone="success", retaining role="status" rather than replacing it with an urgent alert or plain paragraph.

Scenario 2 — Saved data and audit survive reload

Given an allowed event edit succeeds When the record reloads and I reopen it Then the changed value is retained and its existing activity-log entry remains available, with no extra save or audit write caused by rendering the confirmation.

Scenario 3 — Failure cannot report success

Given a new edit is invalid or its save request fails When I attempt to save Then the existing validation or error feedback remains and no success Alert claims that attempt was saved; starting a new edit clears the previous save confirmation.

Scenario 4 — Cancellation and permissions unchanged

Given I cancel an edit or attempt a field I cannot edit under the current event status and access rules When the attempt ends Then cancellation produces no save confirmation or mutation, and existing restrictions and change-request routing remain in force.

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (4 criteria)

  • ☑ Reuse frontend/src/shared/feedback.tsx Alert in frontend/src/features/organiser/ClientEvents.tsx; preserve field-specific text and polite status semantics
  • ☑ Cover successful save/reload/audit, invalid input, failed request after a prior success, cancellation and restricted fields with TC_E03S12_01 to _05
  • ☑ Leave the Coordinator save flow, all other Organiser workflows, permissions and notifications unchanged; no redesign or new notification
  • ☑ Obtain human review of code and test cases and future manual evidence before claiming delivery; this definition does not execute those cases

Create a multi-session event

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Multi-session event management: creates child sessions under an event envelope per C-107/T-79; venue bookings and equipment attach to sessions."

Known Limitation / Boundary: When session deletion leaves only 1 session, T-108 sync trigger automatically aligns event dates and attendance to match.
BDR Lineage:
C-19 Per-session operational requirements exist, but automatic session-by-session venue splitting rules have not been discussed yet at the moment. C-62 Multi-session will requires it to be setup as different event at the moment and the organiser need to set up multiple events. C-107 Each venue booking is made for a specific date/time window (including setup/turnaround). Equipment reservations match the specific session timing/venue where required. Multiple bookings for the same venue/event across different sessions are supported. T-48 Withdraw the sessions model T-79 Restore Session as a child of Event for Release 1 T-85 Permit event registration with selected Sessions and enforce both Session and event capacity
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-018 Restore Sessions as first-class Event entities

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Sessions hold their own requirements

Given I am creating an event When I add one or more Sessions Then each Session stores its date, time, expected attendance, venue requirements, and equipment requirements beneath the Event

Scenario 2 — Single-session event needs no extra setup

Given my event has one Session When I create it Then the system supports it as a single-session Event without requiring extra registration or lifecycle setup

Scenario 3 — Suitability judged per Session

Given two Sessions have different attendance or requirements When venue suitability is assessed for each Then each assessment uses that Session's own requirements and attendance

Scenario 4 — Session booking is independent

Given one Event uses the same venue for different Sessions When bookings are requested Then each booking is linked to its Session and its own time window; a booking for one Session does not replace another Session's booking

Scenario 5 — Deleted Session releases its booking

Given a Session has a confirmed venue booking When I delete that Session Then the booking is released, Venue Staff are notified, and the deletion is recorded in the activity log

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Add one or more Sessions beneath an Event with their own date, time, attendance, venue and equipment requirements
  • ☑ Create a single-session Event without extra lifecycle steps
  • ☑ Assess venue suitability against each Session independently
  • ☑ Link bookings to the Session whose period they cover
  • ☑ Delete a Session and release its confirmed booking with notification and history

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Venue added and searchable

Given I am adding a venue When I save it with location, capacity, facilities, accessibility features, supported layouts and operating hours Then it becomes searchable by Event Coordinators

Scenario 2 — Capacity drop flags bookings

Given a venue has confirmed bookings When I reduce its capacity below the expected attendance of one of those bookings Then the affected bookings are flagged for review and the assigned Coordinators are notified

Scenario 3 — Venue retired

Given a venue has no future bookings When I retire it Then it no longer appears in search results and its past bookings are retained

Scenario 4 — Retirement blocked by future bookings

Given a venue has future bookings When I attempt to retire it Then retirement is blocked and the blocking bookings are identified

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Add a venue with location, capacity, facilities, accessibility features, supported layouts and operating hours
  • ☑ Update any of those attributes on an existing venue
  • ☑ Confirm a new venue becomes searchable by Event Coordinators
  • ☑ Confirm affected bookings are flagged when capacity drops below a booked attendance
  • ☑ Retire a venue that has no future bookings
  • ☑ Be blocked from retiring a venue with future bookings, with those bookings identified

Technical Slice Architecture

Route / Endpoint: GET /api/venues, POST /api/venues, PATCH /api/venues?id=<id>
Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/venueBooking/catalogue.ts
Database Migration: 0001_connectsphere_schema.sql
Frontend Component: frontend/src/features/venue/VenueCatalogue.tsx

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Layout and capacity stored

Scenario 2 — Undersized layout excluded

Given an event requires a theatre layout for a given attendance When a Coordinator searches for venues Then venues whose theatre capacity is below that attendance are excluded or marked unsuitable

Scenario 3 — Duplicate layout warned

Given a layout already exists on the venue When I try to add it again Then I am warned and no duplicate is created

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ View the layouts supported by a venue and their maximum capacities
  • ☑ Add one or more room layouts to a venue
  • ☑ Set and edit a maximum capacity for each layout
  • ☑ Remove a layout no longer offered at the venue
  • ☑ Be warned when adding a layout that already exists

E05-S05 SCRUM-44 Sprint 3 5 pts Aaron Koh ✅ Done

Apply setup and turnaround time

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Venue Staff configures per-venue whole-minute setup and turnaround buffers (C-65, T-66), expanding booking occupancy windows."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Exclusion constraints in Postgres enforce [start - setup, end + turnaround]; maintenance blocks do not get buffered (T-80).
BDR Lineage:
C-65 ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed. Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Buffers recorded on the venue

Given I am creating or editing a venue When I enter a setup time and a turnaround time in whole minutes, either of which may be 0, and save Then both values are stored against the venue and shown on its detail, and every venue that existed before this story has both values at 0

Scenario 2 — Occupancy window computed from the buffers

Given a venue has a setup time of 30 minutes and a turnaround time of 45 minutes When a booking or tentative hold for 10:00 to 12:00 is evaluated for availability or conflicts Then the venue is treated as occupied from 09:30 to 12:45

Scenario 3 — Calendar shows the buffered window

Given a venue with non-zero buffers has a Confirmed booking or a Tentative hold When a Coordinator or Venue Staff member views the venue availability calendar Then the Confirmed or Tentative period shown covers the buffered window and the buffer portion is visually distinguishable from the advertised event time, and the Free, Tentative, Confirmed and Blocked states of E05-S03 are otherwise unchanged

Scenario 4 — Conflicts created by a buffer change are identified, not removed

Given a venue has Confirmed bookings 10:00 to 12:00 and 12:30 to 14:00 and a turnaround time of 0 When I change the turnaround time to 45 minutes and save Then the save succeeds (assumes O-21), both bookings remain Confirmed and the later one is marked Conflicting rather than released, the conflicting pair is listed to me on save, the calendar flags the conflict, and the Coordinator of each affected event is notified (assumes O-20)

Scenario 5 — Buffers do not apply against a maintenance block

Given a venue has a maintenance block ending at 12:00 and a setup time of 30 minutes When a booking request for 12:00 to 14:00 is evaluated Then the block and the booking are compared on the booking's advertised times, so the request is not in conflict with the block (assumes O-22)

Scenario 6 — Adjacent buffered windows do not conflict

Given booking A occupies a venue until 12:45 once its turnaround is applied When booking B's buffered window on the same venue starts at exactly 12:45 Then there is no conflict, and when it starts at 12:44 there is

Scenario 7 — Buffered occupancy excludes a venue from search

Given a venue's existing booking or hold, once that venue's setup and turnaround time are applied, overlaps an event's requested period When a Coordinator runs the venue search for that event Then the venue does not appear as available even though the advertised event times do not overlap; E06-S01 is Done and is not edited, this is its buffered-search requirement placed here under T-74

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Record a setup time and a turnaround time in whole minutes for each venue, with 0 allowed and 0 the default for existing venues
  • ☑ See both values on the venue's detail
  • ☑ Have the calendar, venue search, booking request, booking decision, tentative hold and double-booking prevention all evaluate the buffered occupancy window instead of the advertised event times
  • ☑ See the conflicts a buffer change creates listed on save and flagged on the calendar, with the affected Coordinators notified
  • ☑ Never have a booking released automatically because a buffer changed

E05-S06 SCRUM-152 Sprint 3 8 pts Lexin Phun ✅ Done

Mark a venue temporarily unavailable over existing bookings

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"A venue block can be created over confirmed bookings without being blocked: the block saves, overlapping bookings become Conflicting, and confirmed events return to Planning for resolution (C-119, T-80, T-81)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Block edits retain full history (T-91); lifting blocks notifies affected coordinators without silently resurrecting replaced bookings.
BDR Lineage:
C-66 ConnectSphere needs Venue Staff to be able to mark a venue temporarily unavailable because of maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concerns, or other operational reasons. This may occur even when future events have already been booked at the venue. When this happens, the existing event itself should not automatically be cancelled. Instead, affected bookings should be identified and the relevant Event Coordinators informed that alternative arrangements are required. The system should preserve the original event information while allowing the coordinator to search for and request a replacement venue. C-48 Significant changes (pax, venue, duration) trigger a re-request/notification to the coordinator, but status transitions are not automated. C-61 Venue Staff update venue availability when operational changes occur, triggering a notification to the Event Coordinator to re-evaluate arrangements. While the event status remains visible, the system notifies relevant stakeholders of the venue issue so the coordinator can initiate changes. The co-ordinator will contact the Organiser, liaise about the changes offline and reach an agreement with the organiser. Subsequently the co-ordinator will make relevant changes to the event according to the agreement. C-111 Yes. Marking a venue unavailable for hold blocks new holds and bookings, and flags affected existing bookings so alternative venues can be arranged. It should not be open-ended C-120 Should revert to Planning review. The event itself is preserve and not automatically cancelled. Affected Coordinators are notified to find replacement venues, reverting the status to planning/change review. C-121 The Event Coordinator is informed immediately to arrange alternative venues working with the organiser; Organisers and Attendees are notified when replacement arrangements or formal event changes are confirmed. C-122 If the booking is still active and hasn't been replaced or cancelled, clearing unavailability resolves the conflict; if replaced, new bookings stand. T-28 The Coordinator may revert Confirmed to Planning T-67 Deliver Change 2 as a new E05 story that withdraws E05-S04's refusal of blocks over confirmed bookings, and return E10-S05 to Release 1 T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied T-80 Allow open-ended venue blocks and keep buffers off maintenance blocks T-81 A venue loss returns a Confirmed event to Planning and notifies its Coordinator T-91 Allow Venue Staff to edit venue blocks and retain history O-23 O-24 O-25 O-26
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-011 Controlled vocabularies for accessibility and facilities

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Unavailability recorded with a reason

Given I am viewing a venue When I mark it unavailable from a start date and time, with an optional end date and time, and choose a reason category from maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concern or other, with a free-text note Then the unavailability is saved with the period, the category, the note and my identity, and the calendar shows the period as Blocked; with no end, it shows as Blocked from its start until it is lifted (T-80)

Scenario 2 — Overlapping bookings become Conflicting, not released

Given the venue has a Pending request and a Confirmed booking inside the period When I save the unavailability Then the save succeeds, both bookings are marked Conflicting, neither is released or cancelled, and the two affected events are listed to me on save; overlap is judged on each booking's advertised times, not its setup and turnaround buffers (T-80); an unexpired Tentative hold inside the period is flagged Conflicting in the same way, is not released, and its event is listed and its Coordinator notified as in Scenario 4 (C-111)

Scenario 3 — A Confirmed event returns to Planning, not cancelled

Given a Confirmed event's active venue booking has just become Conflicting When the unavailability is saved Then the event returns to Planning automatically and is not cancelled, every other arrangement is intact, and a venue-conflict flag with the reason category is shown on the event; an affected event that was not Confirmed keeps its status (C-120, T-81)

Scenario 4 — Affected Coordinators informed

Given the unavailability made one or more bookings Conflicting When it is saved Then the Coordinator of each affected event immediately receives an in-app and email notification naming the venue, the period, the reason category and the event, and stating that alternative arrangements are required; the Organiser and registered Attendees are not notified at this point (C-121, T-81)

Scenario 5 — Open-ended or extended unavailability

Given I am recording an unavailability When I leave the end date and time empty Then it is saved as open-ended and stays in force until it is lifted; and Given a saved unavailability When I extend its end or remove its end Then bookings newly inside the longer period are handled as in Scenarios 2 to 4 (T-80, T-91)

Scenario 6 — Unavailability shortened, lifted or ended early

Given a booking is Conflicting only because of an unavailability When I shorten or lift that unavailability so the booking no longer overlaps it Then the Conflicting flag clears and the booking returns to the status it had before, Pending, Confirmed or Tentative, except that a hold whose expiry has passed in the meantime becomes Expired (E06-S05); a booking the Coordinator has already cancelled or replaced is not restored; an event already returned to Planning follows E08-S04 Scenario 4 rather than returning straight to Confirmed (C-122, T-81)

Scenario 7 — Edits and lifts keep their history

Given an unavailability exists When I edit its period or reason, or lift it Then a history entry keeps the earlier and new period and reason with my identity and the time, a lifted unavailability is kept rather than deleted, and when it is lifted the Coordinator of each event whose booking it made Conflicting is notified (T-91)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Mark a venue unavailable from a start date and time, with an optional end, a reason category and a note, including when Pending or Confirmed bookings fall inside the period
  • ☑ See the affected events listed on save and their bookings and unexpired holds marked Conflicting, with none released or cancelled
  • ☑ Confirm an affected Confirmed event returns to Planning without being cancelled, keeps its other arrangements and shows a venue-conflict flag
  • ☑ Confirm each affected Coordinator is notified in-app and by email, and the Organiser and registered Attendees are not
  • ☑ Save an open-ended unavailability, and extend an existing one so bookings newly inside it are flagged
  • ☑ Confirm shortening or lifting an unavailability clears the Conflicting flag on bookings it no longer touches and restores their earlier status
  • ☑ Confirm each edit and lift keeps a history entry, and a lift notifies the affected Coordinators
  • ☑ Confirm E05-S04's existing block, shorten and remove behaviour still works for periods with no bookings

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Suitability shown for the event

Given an event has recorded requirements When I view a venue in the context of the event Then a suitability status is shown for the event

Scenario 2 — Failing requirements named

Given a venue fails one or more recorded requirements When I view it Then it is marked unsuitable and every failing requirement is named

Scenario 3 — All requirements met

Given a venue meets all recorded requirements for the event When I view it Then it is marked suitable

Scenario 4 — Unsuitable venue may still be requested

Given a venue is marked unsuitable When I submit a booking request for it anyway Then the request is accepted and the unsuitability is shown to the Venue Staff for their decision

Scenario 5 - Operating hours checked without blocking booking (T-77)

Given an event has recorded start and end times When I check a venue's suitability Then an event outside the venue's operating hours is marked Unsuitable with "outside operating hours" explicitly named; an event fully within the hours passes this criterion. Suitability remains advisory and an unsuitable venue may still be requested, with its failures shown to Venue Staff for their decision. Product Owner clarification relayed on 8 October 2026. E06-S01 operating hours remain display-only; its search behaviour is unchanged. Use the existing Singapore timezone and daily opening-window convention. Exact opening and closing times are within hours. This is event-based; T-21's sessions wording is withdrawn by T-48.

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ View a suitability status for a venue against a specific event
  • ☑ See the venue marked unsuitable when it fails one or more recorded requirements
  • ☑ See every failing requirement named
  • ☑ See the venue marked suitable when it meets all recorded requirements
  • ☑ Confirm suitability is advisory and does not itself block a booking request
  • ☑ Identify outside operating hours as an advisory failure in E06-S02, without adding that rule to E06-S01
