E06-S03 SCRUM-47 Sprint 3 3 pts Ji Ning Yee ✅ Done

Request a venue booking

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Coordinator requests venue booking or withdraws pending request; multiple bookings allowed per event (T-68), first request transitions to Planning."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Withdrawal locks venue row FOR NO KEY UPDATE then booking FOR UPDATE (T-95); Released bookings permit fresh replacement requests (T-96).
BDR Lineage:
C-01 1. Tentative hold duration does not matter for now. 2. Rejections should not be overridden 3. Venues are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. C-16 Tentative hold duration does not matter at the moment since it has not been prioritised, and confirmed venue bookings operate on a first-come, first-served basis without manual overrides. C-17 Two events cannot hold the same venue tentatively at the same time, but holding multiple options for one event is left to coordinator workflow design by the system. C-37 Holding rules do not matter for now; two events cannot hold the same venue tentatively at the same time. C-46 Venue allocation is handled strictly on a first-come, first-served basis. C-60 Tentative holding itself is in scope (limited to only one active tentative hold or confirmed booking should exist for a venue/time slot). Specific auto-expiry rules, durations, and placing multiple candidate venues on hold simultaneously are not required/specified for Release 1 and can be proposed by the team if the team feels that it adds value to the organisation. T-20 One pending venue request per session at a time T-49 Bring tentative holding into Release 1 C-65 ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed. T-66 Return E05-S05 to Release 1 with per-venue setup and turnaround buffers C-67 ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required. T-68 Retire T-20 and allow several venue bookings per event, each checked independently T-78 Confirm per-booking requirements, primary venue, request eligibility and hold conversion O-27 O-29 O-30 T-94 Limit E06-S03 withdrawal to Pending requests; separate Confirmed cancellation T-95 Reuse Released and serialize withdrawal with staff decisions; notify the requested venue's staff T-96 Allow replacement retry after withdrawal, but follow the latest rejection's suggestion after rejection
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-013 Separate the backlog data from the reasoning behind it ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

Decision-first leaves Confirmed or Rejected and withdrawal returns 409 with refresh guidance. Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

Happy Path Acceptance (IS212 Step 2)

Scenario: Notify only the withdrawn request's current venue staff and retain conversion hi

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

PostgreSQL GiST exclusion constraint (0016 tsrange guard), FOR UPDATE row-level booking lock, or the 48-hour hold expiration worker.

Pre-conditions: A Pending request converted from a hold exists; its requested venue has current active Venue Staff assignments. Other bookings have different staff; expired/inactive assignments also exist.

Steps: 1. Withdraw the converted Pending request. 2. Inspect venue occupancy, the original row, its audit, staff inbox and email outbox. 3. Inspect other bookings and recipients. 4. With an injected outbox failure on a separate request, repeat withdrawal.

Expected outcome: Success changes only that request to Released without restoring a hold or expiry. The event status and other bookings stay unchanged. Only the requested venue's currently assigned active Venue Staff receive the withdrawal notice, deduplicated; no unrelated venue or inactive staff is notified. Audit identifies actor, booking, event and Pending to Released. An outbox failure rolls back booking/audit/notifications together; persisted outbox is not proof of provider receipt.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

Retained Released history does not consume the slot.

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Request created as Pending

Given an event has recorded requirements and no pending request When I submit a booking request for a venue Then the request is created with status Pending, the venue calendar shows the period as Tentative, and the Venue Staff are notified

Scenario 2 — First request moves event to Planning

Given the event has status Approved When its first booking request is submitted Then the event status becomes Planning

Scenario 3 — Several venue bookings for one event

Given the event already has a Pending or Confirmed venue booking When I submit a request for another venue, or for the same venue over a different period, for the same event Then the request is created as Pending alongside the existing bookings, each booking keeps its own status, the event lists all of them, and withdrawing or changing one booking leaves the others untouched (C-67, T-68; replaces the earlier rule that blocked a second request, T-20 retired)

Scenario 4 — Venue taken by another event blocked

Given a venue is already Pending or Confirmed for another event over the same period When I submit a request for it Then submission is blocked and the conflict is explained

Scenario 5 — Request conflicts through the buffer

Given a venue is Confirmed for another event 10:00 to 12:00 and has a turnaround time of 45 minutes When I submit a request for 12:30 to 14:00 Then submission is blocked and the conflict names the other event's buffered window, 09:30 to 12:45 (C-65, T-66) Confirmed-primary cancellation is a future separate flow: clear primary and prompt the Organiser to select another Confirmed venue, with no automatic promotion (T-94). This does not implement that flow or change the existing Coordinator selection permission in Scenario 3c.

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (11 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit a booking request only as the assigned Event Coordinator while the event is Approved or Planning, using its recorded requirements (T-78)
  • ☑ Confirm the request is created as Pending and Venue Staff are notified
  • ☑ Confirm the venue calendar shows the period as Tentative
  • ☑ Confirm the event status moves from Approved to Planning on the first request
  • ☑ Hold several venue bookings, Pending or Confirmed, for one event, each with an optional purpose and headcount, and mark one as primary (C-67; confirmed O-27 and O-30, T-78)
  • ☑ Be blocked from requesting a venue already Pending or Confirmed for another event in that period, counting that venue's setup and turnaround time (C-65)
  • ☑ View the status of each of my booking requests
  • ☑ Withdraw only a Pending request to Released, preserving other bookings and the event status; notify the requested venue's assigned staff (T-94, T-95)
  • ☑ Serialize withdrawal against approval/rejection and retain the booking-specific audit history (T-95)
  • ☑ Allow a new replacement after withdrawal; after rejection follow only the latest rejection's own suggestion (T-96)
  • ☑ Complete TC_E06S03_09 to _13 under the current Sprint 3 plan; record anything unfinished honestly at sprint close (PO confirmation, 16 October; T-94)

E06-S04 SCRUM-48 Sprint 3 3 pts Lexin Phun ✅ Done

Decide on a venue booking request

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Venue Staff approves or rejects booking requests with optional alternative venue suggestions (C-08); writes immutable audit entries (T-76)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Approval serializes via FOR UPDATE locks, rechecking that the buffered window has not been claimed concurrently (T-100).
BDR Lineage:
C-08 Venue staff can suggest an alternative arrangement; the Event Coordinator adjusts the venue booking request based on the suggestion without restarting the full planning process. T-39 A rejection reason is mandatory C-65 ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed. T-66 Return E05-S05 to Release 1 with per-venue setup and turnaround buffers T-75 Event Coordinators read the event Activity log; no Administrator role in Release 1 T-76 Move booking-decision logging to E06-S04 and carry remaining E14-S02 work to Sprint 3
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-013 Separate the backlog data from the reasoning behind it ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Request approved and confirmed

Given a booking request is pending and the venue is free for the period When I approve it Then the booking becomes Confirmed, the venue calendar is updated and the Coordinator is notified

Scenario 2 — Rejected with reason and alternative

Given I reject a request When I record a reason and optionally suggest an alternative venue Then the Coordinator is notified with both, and can amend the request to the suggested alternative without restarting the search

Scenario 3 — Rejection without reason blocked

Given I attempt to reject without recording a reason When I confirm Then the rejection is blocked

Scenario 4 — Approval checks the buffered window

Given approving a pending request would make its buffered occupancy window overlap another Confirmed booking's buffered window on the same venue When I approve it Then approval is blocked and the conflicting booking is identified, even if the two advertised event times do not overlap (C-65, T-66)

Scenario 5 — Booking decision recorded

Given a venue booking is approved, rejected or released When the action completes Then an entry is recorded with the actor, the action, the affected records and the time

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (9 criteria)

  • ☑ Approve a pending booking request for a free venue
  • ☑ Confirm the booking becomes Confirmed and the calendar updates
  • ☑ Reject a request with a recorded reason
  • ☑ Be blocked from rejecting without a reason
  • ☑ Suggest an alternative venue alongside a rejection
  • ☑ Confirm the Coordinator can amend the request to the suggested venue without starting a new search
  • ☑ Confirm the Coordinator is notified of either decision
  • ☑ Record each booking approval, rejection and release with actor, action, affected booking/event and time in the same transaction as the action
  • ☑ Verify all three booking-log outcomes under TC_E06S04_05, TC_E06S04_06 and TC_E06S04_07

E06-S05 SCRUM-49 Sprint 3 5 pts Amareet Kaur (Scrum Master) ✅ Done

Hold a venue tentatively

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Coordinator places tentative holds occupying buffered windows; shipped code follows T-92 (48h default, 1h-14d custom, unlimited logged extensions)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Hold ceases occupying venue immediately at clock_timestamp() (T-92); converting hold to booking request ends expiry timer (T-78).
BDR Lineage:
C-01 1. Tentative hold duration does not matter for now. 2. Rejections should not be overridden 3. Venues are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. C-16 Tentative hold duration does not matter at the moment since it has not been prioritised, and confirmed venue bookings operate on a first-come, first-served basis without manual overrides. C-37 Holding rules do not matter for now; two events cannot hold the same venue tentatively at the same time. C-60 Tentative holding itself is in scope (limited to only one active tentative hold or confirmed booking should exist for a venue/time slot). Specific auto-expiry rules, durations, and placing multiple candidate venues on hold simultaneously are not required/specified for Release 1 and can be proposed by the team if the team feels that it adds value to the organisation. T-49 Bring tentative holding into Release 1 C-65 ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed. T-66 Return E05-S05 to Release 1 with per-venue setup and turnaround buffers C-68 Venue Staff have explained that they sometimes temporarily hold a venue while an Event Coordinator is finalising event arrangements. These tentative holds should not reserve a venue indefinitely. Each hold must therefore have an expiry date/time. If the required action is not completed before the deadline, the hold should expire and the venue should become available for other requests. The Event Coordinator should be informed before or when the hold expires, and an expired hold should not be treated as a confirmed booking. T-69 Amend T-49: every tentative hold carries an expiry and is expired by the system T-78 Confirm per-booking requirements, primary venue, request eligibility and hold conversion T-92 Settle E06-S05's remaining hold defaults: 48-hour expiry, unlimited logged extensions, one notice at expiry O-31 O-32 O-33 O-34 T-102 A refused hold names only the unavailable buffered window, not the other event
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-013 Separate the backlog data from the reasoning behind it ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

Standalone immutable postplan verification artifact recording DoD criteria, reviewer sign-offs, and evidence.

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Tentative hold placed

Given a venue is free for the period When I place a tentative hold Then the calendar shows the period as Tentative, the hold is recorded against my event, and the hold carries an expiry date and time set to 48 hours from creation by default, which Venue Staff may change on the hold (assumes O-31)

Scenario 2 — Slot already held or booked

Given a venue already has a tentative hold or a confirmed booking for the period When I attempt to hold it for another event Then the hold is refused and the occupied buffered window is shown as unavailable, without naming the other event (T-102)

Scenario 3 — Hold becomes a booking request

Given I hold a venue tentatively When I submit a booking request for that venue Then the hold becomes a pending booking request for the same period and the expiry no longer applies, because submitting the request is the action that completes the hold; an expired hold cannot be converted (confirmed O-32, T-78)

Scenario 4 — Hold released

Given I hold a venue tentatively and no longer need it When I release the hold Then the period returns to Free on the calendar

Scenario 5 — Hold occupies the buffered window

Given a venue has a setup time of 30 minutes and a turnaround time of 45 minutes When I hold it tentatively for 10:00 to 12:00 Then the hold occupies 09:30 to 12:45, the calendar shows that window as Tentative, and another hold or booking request overlapping any part of it is refused (C-65, T-66)

Scenario 6 — Hold expires and frees the venue

Given my hold's expiry date and time has passed and I have not submitted a booking request for it When the expiry job next runs Then the hold's status becomes Expired, the period returns to Free on the calendar, the venue can be held or requested by any event, and an Expired hold is never counted as a Confirmed or Pending booking anywhere, including the E08-S03 confirmation gate (C-68, T-69)

Scenario 7 — Coordinator told at expiry

Given my hold expires When the expiry job runs Then I receive one in-app notice and one email naming the venue, the event and the expiry time, saying the hold has expired and the venue is free; a later run sends nothing more. There is no reminder before expiry (T-92, replacing the O-33 default)

Scenario 8 — Venue Staff may extend a hold

Given a hold has not yet expired When Venue Staff set a later expiry date and time Then the new expiry applies, and the extension is recorded in the activity log with who made it; an expired hold cannot be extended and must be placed again (T-92)

Scenario 9 — Expiry exactly at the boundary

Given a hold expires at 10:00:00 When the expiry job runs at 09:59:59 Then the hold is still Tentative, and when it runs at 10:00:00 or later Then the hold is Expired

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (10 criteria)

  • ☑ Place a tentative hold on a venue that is free for the period
  • ☑ See the period shown as Tentative on the venue calendar
  • ☑ Be refused when the slot already has a tentative hold or a confirmed booking for another event
  • ☑ Convert a tentative hold into a booking request
  • ☑ Release a tentative hold, returning the period to Free
  • ☑ Confirm only one active hold or confirmed booking exists per venue and period
  • ☑ See the expiry date and time on every hold, defaulting to 48 hours after creation (assumes O-31)
  • ☑ Confirm an expired hold frees the venue and is never treated as a booking
  • ☑ Receive one notice, in-app and by email, when a hold expires (T-92)
  • ☑ Confirm Venue Staff can extend an unexpired hold and the extension is logged (assumes O-34)

Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/venueBooking/holds.ts

E06-S06 SCRUM-50 Sprint 3 5 pts Lexin Phun ✅ Done

Prevent double-booking of a venue

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Prevents booking race and double-booking: PostgreSQL exclusion constraint blocks overlapping holds or bookings across buffered occupancy windows (T-100). First accepted claim wins under Rule B."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Losing concurrent request returns 409 Conflict with clear buffered window timeframe without leaking competing event titles (T-102).
BDR Lineage:
C-01 1. Tentative hold duration does not matter for now. 2. Rejections should not be overridden 3. Venues are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. C-16 Tentative hold duration does not matter at the moment since it has not been prioritised, and confirmed venue bookings operate on a first-come, first-served basis without manual overrides. C-46 Venue allocation is handled strictly on a first-come, first-served basis. T-22 Consolidate conflict logic into E06-S06 C-60 Tentative holding itself is in scope (limited to only one active tentative hold or confirmed booking should exist for a venue/time slot). Specific auto-expiry rules, durations, and placing multiple candidate venues on hold simultaneously are not required/specified for Release 1 and can be proposed by the team if the team feels that it adds value to the organisation. C-65 ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed. T-66 Return E05-S05 to Release 1 with per-venue setup and turnaround buffers C-67 ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required. T-68 Retire T-20 and allow several venue bookings per event, each checked independently C-109 Existing bookings that become problematic under new buffer rules are identified and flagged for review rather than silently removed or hard-rejected on save. The coirdinator has the final approval based on his assessment. T-100 PO interpretation: the first accepted hold or request claims its buffered venue slot; approval rechecks current conditions T-102 A refused hold names only the unavailable buffered window, not the other event
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database

TC_E06S06_01 — Verify approval rechecks a confirmed booking after buffer growth
Negative Guardrail / Business Rule (IS212 Step 4)

Scenario: Verify approval rechecks a confirmed booking after buffer growth

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Validates defensive exception handling and business rule enforcement. As emphasized in IS212 Week 4 Slide 26 and Week 6, this test proves the system rejects invalid inputs or unauthorized operations with predictable error responses (HTTP 4xx), protecting database consistency (E06-S06 - Scenario 4 (Approval rechecks current buffered availability; T-100)).

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

PostgreSQL GiST exclusion constraint (0016 tsrange guard), FOR UPDATE row-level booking lock, or the 48-hour hold expiration worker.

Pre-conditions: Venue Orchid Hall has setup and turnaround set to 0. Confirmed booking Charity Run occupies 09:00-11:00 and Pending request Product Expo occupies 11:00-13:00; both were accepted while their advertised periods were adjacent. Venue Staff then changes setup time to 30 minutes.

Steps: 1. Confirm the buffer edit saves and both bookings remain present; Pending Product Expo has buffer_conflict true while Confirmed Charity Run remains unflagged. 2. Open Product Expo's Pending request and attempt approval.

Expected outcome: Approval of Product Expo is refused after checking current buffers. Confirmed Charity Run and Pending Product Expo are both retained; Charity Run remains unflagged and Product Expo carries buffer_conflict true.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

TC_E06S06_06 — Verify buffer-growth conflicts block approvals until an explicit resolution
Integration & State Integrity (IS212 Week 9)

Scenario: Verify buffer-growth conflicts block approvals until an explicit resolution

🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

Tests cross-boundary persistence and relational cascades against real PostgreSQL (avoiding the 'mock-based integration illusion', Week 9 Slide 20). Verifies rollback semantics under failure for E06-S06 - Scenario 4 (Approval rechecks current buffered availability; T-100).

💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

PostgreSQL GiST exclusion constraint (0016 tsrange guard), FOR UPDATE row-level booking lock, or the 48-hour hold expiration worker.

Pre-conditions: Orchid Hall has setup and turnaround set to 0. Two Pending requests, Charity Run 10:00-12:00 and Alumni Dinner 12:00-14:00, were successfully accepted while their advertised windows were adjacent. Venue Staff then changes setup to 30 minutes and turnaround to 45 minutes.

Steps: 1. Confirm the buffer edit saves and both Pending rows remain; earlier Charity Run is unflagged and later Alumni Dinner has buffer_conflict true under the existing equal-status ordering. 2. Attempt approval of each request while the buffered conflict remains. 3. Resolve the conflict using one of these paths: (primary) Venue Staff reject one conflicting Pending request with a reason; (alternative) an authorized Coordinator withdraws/replans one request to a nonconflicting period and resubmits it as needed. 4. Approve the remaining now-free Pending request. For the alternative path, also approve the replanned request only if it is Pending and conflict-free.

Expected outcome: Both approvals are refused while the conflict remains, and there is no automatic winner. Equal-status ordering leaves earlier Charity Run unflagged and sets buffer_conflict true on later Alumni Dinner. The primary resolution is for Venue Staff to reject one conflicting Pending request with a reason; that row becomes terminal Rejected, and the remaining still-Pending request can then be approved. Alternatively, an authorized Coordinator may withdraw/replan one request to a nonconflicting period; the remaining now-free Pending request and any valid replanned Pending request can then be approved. A Rejected row is never approved.

Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — First accepted claim reserves the buffered slot

Given a venue has no active overlapping Pending, Confirmed or unexpired Tentative booking When a hold or booking request is successfully accepted Then its current buffered window is claimed for that venue

Scenario 2 — Later overlapping claim refused

Given an active claim reserves a venue's buffered window When another hold or booking request overlaps it Then the new claim is refused, the ordinary Coordinator response identifies the occupied buffered window as unavailable without disclosing another event's title or private booking details, and the active claim remains unchanged

Scenario 3 — Concurrent claims fail safely

Given two new holds or booking requests concurrently claim overlapping buffered windows on one venue When both are processed Then exactly one claim is accepted and the other receives 409 without an extra row or side effects

Scenario 4 — Approval rechecks current buffered availability

Given a request was accepted while its buffered window was available and the venue buffers later change When Venue Staff attempt approval Then current availability, concurrency and buffer values are rechecked; C-109 conflicts stay flagged and retained, and approval is blocked until Venue Staff reject one conflicting Pending request with a reason or an authorized Coordinator withdraws/replans one request. The remaining now-free Pending request may then be approved; a Rejected request is terminal and is never approved. No claim is silently released or selected as a winner. Exactly adjacent half-open buffered windows remain available.

Scenario 5 — Conflicts are per venue, not per event

Given one event has claims on two different venues over the same period When both requests are approved Then both become Confirmed, because conflict detection is per venue and an event may legitimately occupy several venues at once (C-67, T-68)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm the first successfully accepted hold or request claims its venue's buffered slot
  • ☑ Be refused a later overlapping hold or request while the first claim remains active
  • ☑ Confirm concurrent overlapping new claims yield one accepted claim and one 409 with no extra row or side effects
  • ☑ Recheck current availability, concurrency and buffer values at approval
  • ☑ Retain and flag bookings under C-109 after a later buffer change; block approval while the conflict remains
  • ☑ Resolve a conflict explicitly by rejection, withdrawal or replan before a later approval succeeds
  • ☑ Allow exact adjacency of half-open buffered windows and refuse a one-minute overlap
  • ☑ Confirm conflicts are per venue, so one event may confirm overlapping bookings on different venues

E06-S07 SCRUM-260 - **Points**: 5 5 pts Ji Ning Yee ⚠️ Partial (Gate Incomplete)

Configure tentative-hold expiry and warning

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"First confirmed venue automatically becomes primary; coordinator may designate another confirmed venue as primary (T-78)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Pending or unconfirmed venues cannot be marked primary; primary designation dictates public attendee display (E09-S01).
BDR Lineage:
C-68 Venue Staff have explained that they sometimes temporarily hold a venue while an Event Coordinator is finalising event arrangements. These tentative holds should not reserve a venue indefinitely. Each hold must therefore have an expiry date/time. If the required action is not completed before the deadline, the hold should expire and the venue should become available for other requests. The Event Coordinator should be informed before or when the hold expires, and an expired hold should not be treated as a confirmed booking. C-79 The Venue Staff specify the expiry date/time per hold based on their knowledge. System notifies/warns the Coordinator before or when the hold expires. The warning time can be set by the coordinator per event hold. C-96 When the tentative hold expires, the venue becomes available for other requests. An expired hold cannot be treated as confirmed; the Coordinator must submit a new request if needed. C-99 Venue Staff specify the expiry date/time per hold based on venue knowledge; length is not fixed by the system. C-110 Venue Staff can set and update/extend the hold expiry duration in the system as necessary. He need to notify the event coordinator with such changes. C-114 Venue Staff set and update the hold expiry date/time upon receiving the booking/hold request from the Coordinator. C-124 Venue Staff set/update the expiry date/time per hold based on venue knowledge. C-125 Week 7 Changes.docx requires informing the Event Coordinator before or when the hold expires via notifications. C-126 Venue Staff have the authority to update and set the hold duration as appropriate. T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied
Architectural Decisions:
ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-013 Separate the backlog data from the reasoning behind it ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Venue Staff set the hold expiry

Given a Coordinator requests a tentative hold for a free venue and period When the responsible Venue Staff set an expiry date and time for that hold Then the resulting Tentative hold records that staff-configured expiry and reserves its venue window; no fixed default duration is applied

Scenario 2 — No active hold without a configured expiry

Given no Venue Staff expiry has been set for a requested hold When the request is viewed or another booking is checked Then it is not represented as an active Tentative hold or an indefinite reservation

Scenario 3 — Coordinator chooses the warning time

Given a Tentative hold has a staff-configured expiry When the Coordinator sets a warning time for that hold Then the system records that warning for the hold and notifies the Coordinator before or at expiry according to the configured time

Scenario 4 — Expiry frees the venue

Given a configured hold reaches its expiry without becoming a booking request When the expiry processing runs Then the hold becomes Expired, the venue window is freed, and a Coordinator who still needs it must submit a new request

Scenario 5 — Venue Staff update an unexpired hold

Given a Tentative hold has not expired When Venue Staff update its expiry Then the new expiry applies and the Coordinator is notified of the change; the update does not create a second hold for the same reservation

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Set an explicit per-hold expiry as Venue Staff; do not apply a fixed default
  • ☑ Refuse to treat an unconfigured request as an indefinite active hold
  • ☑ Set a per-hold Coordinator warning and notify before or at expiry
  • ☑ Expire an unused hold, free the venue, and require a new request if needed
  • ☑ Update an unexpired hold as Venue Staff and notify the Coordinator

    • ☑ Confirm retired items no longer appear in availability checks

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Reserved and faulty stock excluded

    Given some items are reserved for other events in the period When I check availability Then the free quantity excludes those reservations and any items marked damaged or under maintenance

    Scenario 2 — Location does not affect availability

    Given an item is free for the requested date and time but is currently located at another venue When I check availability Then it is shown as available and no transport allowance is applied

    Scenario 3 — Non-overlapping events share an item

    Given two events require the same item at non-overlapping times on the same day When I check availability Then the item is free for both

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

    • ☑ View the free quantity of an item for a given date and time
    • ☑ Confirm reservations for other events are excluded from the free quantity
    • ☑ Confirm damaged or under-maintenance items are excluded
    • ☑ Confirm items at other venues are still counted as available
    • ☑ Confirm the same item can serve two events at non-overlapping times

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Full reservation recorded

    Given sufficient equipment is free for the period When I reserve the requested quantity Then the reservation is recorded against the event and the Event Coordinator is notified

    Scenario 2 — Partial reservation and shortfall

    Given only part of the requested quantity is free When I record a partial reservation Then the Coordinator is notified of the shortfall and the outstanding quantity

    Scenario 3 — Fully committed item shows nothing free

    Given an item becomes fully committed When availability is next checked for that period Then no free quantity is shown

    Scenario 4 — Reservation released

    Given an event is cancelled or its equipment is no longer required When I release the reservation Then the quantity returns to the available pool

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Select an event and equipment item to reserve
    • ☑ Specify the quantity required
    • ☑ See an error when the requested quantity exceeds what is available
    • ☑ Record a partial reservation and notify the Coordinator of the shortfall
    • ☑ Release a reservation when an event is cancelled or the equipment is no longer needed
    • ☑ Receive confirmation showing the event, date, time, item and quantity

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Available colleague assigned

    Given an event has an open technical support request and a colleague is available for its times When I assign them Then they are notified and the assignment appears on their schedule

    Scenario 2 — Overlapping assignment blocked

    Given a colleague is already assigned to another event at an overlapping time When I try to assign them Then the assignment is blocked and the conflicting event is identified

    Scenario 3 — Assignment removed

    Given an assignment exists When I remove it Then the colleague is notified and the slot is freed

    Scenario 4 — Replacement assigned under same check

    Given I have removed an assignment When I assign a replacement Then the same conflict check is applied

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Assign a colleague only when they have no conflicting assignment the event's period
    • ☑ See the assignment on the assigned staff member's schedule
    • ☑ Be blocked from assigning a colleague with an overlapping assignment, with the conflicting event identified
    • ☑ Remove an existing assignment
    • ☑ Assign a replacement colleague subject to the same conflict check
    • ☑ Confirm the staff member is notified when assigned or removed

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Request linked to its Session

    Given an Event has multiple Sessions When an Event Coordinator records equipment needed for one Session Then the request is linked to that Session and remains part of the Event

    Scenario 2 — Reservation linked to its Session

    Given a request is approved for reservation When Technical Support Staff reserve equipment Then each reservation identifies the same Session and uses its date/time for availability checks

    Scenario 3 — Cross-event Session rejected

    Given a request belongs to one Event When a Session from a different Event is selected Then the request or reservation is rejected and no cross-event link is saved

    Scenario 4 — Event-level assignment remains

    Given Technical Support Staff are assigned to support an Event When Sessions are added or changed Then the staff assignment remains event-level unless a separate accepted requirement changes it

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (4 criteria)

    • ☑ Record equipment requests against a Session of the owning Event
    • ☑ Reserve equipment against the requested Session and check its period
    • ☑ Reject Session identifiers belonging to another Event
    • ☑ Keep technical-support staff assignment event-level

    TC_E07S09_02 — Withdrawal boundaries and peak demand are respected
    Boundary Value Analysis & EP (IS212 Step 5)

    Scenario: Withdrawal boundaries and peak demand are respected

    🎙️ Why We Chose This Test (Spoken Defense):

    Applies Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) and Equivalence Partitioning (EP) at critical operational thresholds (5 - Boundary). Rather than redundant happy-path testing ('AI coverage theatre', Week 4 Slide 36), this targets the exact boundary where off-by-one errors and race conditions occur (E07-S09 — Scenario 2).

    💥 What Would Have to Be Broken to Fail (First Principles):

    Equipment inventory reservation counters, technician FOR NO KEY UPDATE user row lock (PR #239), or support request assignment logic.

    Pre-conditions: An active item with stock 10 and reservation quantity 5. Each variant uses fresh synthetic data.

    Steps: 1. Reduce stock to 8 with a withdrawal of 4 starting midway through the reservation. 2. Repeat with the withdrawal on another date, ending exactly at the reservation start, starting exactly at its end, or already ended. 3. Repeat with two withdrawals of 2: first non-overlapping, then overlapping inside the reservation.

    Expected outcome: Mid-period withdrawal of 4 and overlapping withdrawals totalling 4 flag the reservation. Unrelated/adjacent/ended withdrawals and separate withdrawals of 2 do not.

    Justification: Acceptance scenario and expected result define the reason for this case.

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Reduced usable stock flags reservations

    Given an item has total stock 10, four units withdrawn and five units reserved for the same future period When I reduce total stock to 8 Then the save succeeds, the reservation remains reserved but is marked for review, and its assigned active Coordinator receives one notification and an outbox record

    Scenario 2 — Only simultaneous remaining demand counts

    Given reservations and dated withdrawals have different or adjacent periods When I reduce total stock Then only simultaneous demand in each reservation's remaining period is compared against the new stock; a withdrawal starting midway through the reservation is included, non-overlapping withdrawal quantities are not summed, and exact fits are not flagged

    Scenario 3 — Notification failure rolls back the edit

    Given a stock reduction would flag a reservation because of a withdrawal When notification persistence fails Then the stock change, new review flag and notification all roll back

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

    • ☑ Include dated withdrawals and their start boundaries in catalogue capacity checks
    • ☑ Preserve half-open adjacency and ignore ended demand
    • ☑ Keep reservations intact while flagging shortages
    • ☑ Notify each affected assigned active Coordinator once per stock edit
    • ☑ Roll back stock, flags and notification/outbox writes together on failure

    Route / Endpoint: POST /api/venues?task=staffing&reconfirm=list, POST ... reconfirm
    Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/equipmentSupport/staffAssignments.ts
    Database Migration: 0026_support_reconfirmation.sql

    Confirm an event

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Coordinator inspects readiness checklist; first-time planning requires manual coordinator submission to enter Safety Review (C-70, T-71)."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: All venue bookings must be Confirmed and technical requirements fulfilled with zero shortfall before submission is enabled.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-13 Both venue and technical support/equipment arrangements must be completed before confirmation. C-39 Coordinators oversee overall planning, but both venue and technical support arrangements are mandatory prior to final confirmation. C-59 Yes. The required arrangements depend on the event's actual needs. If an event does not require equipment, 'none required' is considered fulfilled/complete and will not block confirmation. Furthermore, the Event Coordinator and Technical Support Staff determine which requirements are essential. C-63 The system is designed around ConnectSphere managed venues, and no explicit provision for off-site client premises is detailed in the core requirements. These can be recorded as comments for the event in the system and handled outside of the system. T-02 Bring E08-S03 into release 1 T-24 A partial equipment reservation blocks confirmation T-27 Confirmation requires every session arranged C-67 ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required. T-68 Retire T-20 and allow several venue bookings per event, each checked independently O-28 C-70 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request). T-71 Add a Safety Review gate between Planning and Confirmed as the interim placement of C-70's Operational Safety Check T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied O-39 O-40
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-006 Transactional outbox for notification delivery ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — All arrangements complete, event submitted for safety review

    Given every venue booking on the event is Confirmed or has been withdrawn, at least one is Confirmed, its full requested equipment is reserved and any requested technical support is assigned When I submit the event for its Operational Safety Check Then the status becomes Safety Review, the Safety Officer is notified, the Organiser is told the event is awaiting its safety check, and the event becomes Confirmed only when the Safety Officer approves it (E08-S06) (C-67, T-68, C-70, T-71; assumes O-28, O-39, O-40)

    Scenario 2 — Missing venue blocks submission

    Given the event has no Confirmed venue booking, or any of its venue bookings is still Pending or Conflicting When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked and each outstanding booking is listed by venue (assumes O-28)

    Scenario 3 — Partial equipment blocks submission

    Given the event has only a partial equipment reservation When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked and the outstanding quantity is shown

    Scenario 4 — None required does not block

    Given the event was submitted with 'none required' for equipment When I submit it for safety review Then that requirement counts as fulfilled and does not block submission

    Scenario 5 — Outstanding support assignment blocks submission

    Given the event requested technical support and no staff are assigned When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked

    Scenario 6 — Organiser sees confirmed arrangements

    Given an event has been confirmed When the Event Organiser views it Then every confirmed venue with its purpose and period, the date, time and arrangements are shown

    Scenario 7 — Confirmed is reached only through approval

    Given an event is in Safety Review When anyone other than a Safety Officer attempts to set its status to Confirmed Then the action is refused and recorded in the activity log (C-70, T-71)

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

    • ☑ Submit an event for its Operational Safety Check once every venue booking is Confirmed or withdrawn, equipment is fully reserved and technical support is assigned, moving it to Safety Review with the Safety Officer notified
    • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while the event has no Confirmed venue booking or any booking still Pending or Conflicting, with each one listed (assumes O-28)
    • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while an equipment reservation is partial, with the shortfall shown
    • ☑ Confirm an event whose equipment requirement was recorded as 'none required'
    • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while a requested technical support assignment is outstanding
    • ☑ Confirm the event becomes Confirmed only through the Safety Officer's approval (E08-S06), never directly
    • ☑ Confirm the Event Organiser is notified with the full confirmed details

    Revert a confirmed event to planning

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Coordinator manually reverts Confirmed event to Planning; also auto-triggered on venue loss (T-81); re-enters Safety Review automatically once ready (T-82)."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: Reversion leaves arrangements intact but marks affected items for reconfirmation; event cannot re-confirm without clearing flags.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-48 Significant changes (pax, venue, duration) trigger a re-request/notification to the coordinator, but status transitions are not automated. T-03 Split confirmation into three stories by operation T-28 The Coordinator may revert Confirmed to Planning C-70 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request). T-71 Add a Safety Review gate between Planning and Confirmed as the interim placement of C-70's Operational Safety Check C-120 Should revert to Planning review. The event itself is preserve and not automatically cancelled. Affected Coordinators are notified to find replacement venues, reverting the status to planning/change review. T-81 A venue loss returns a Confirmed event to Planning and notifies its Coordinator C-132 Automatic trigger. Once venue and technical arrangements are confirmed, the event enters the Safety Officer review stage. T-82 Start Safety Review automatically and record both a factor checklist and the decision/comments
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-006 Transactional outbox for notification delivery ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Manual reversion records a reason

    Given an event is Confirmed When I deliberately revert it to Planning and record a reason Then the status becomes Planning and the Event Organiser is notified with the reason

    Scenario 2 — Registered Attendees notified on deliberate reversion

    Given registered Attendees exist When I deliberately revert the event Then they are notified that arrangements are being revised

    Scenario 3 — Other broken arrangements remain flagged

    Given a non-venue arrangement breaks on a Confirmed event When the owning workflow flags it Then the affected arrangement is flagged and the Coordinator can use the deliberate reversion workflow; venue-block loss follows Scenario 5

    Scenario 4 — Arrangements reconfirmed and safety review starts automatically

    Given a reverted event has all required venue and technical arrangements confirmed again When the final required arrangement is confirmed Then the event enters Safety Review automatically, the Safety Officer is notified, and the previous safety decision remains in history but is not reused (C-132, T-82)

    Scenario 5 — Venue loss automatically returns event to Planning

    Given a block makes a Confirmed event's active venue booking unavailable When the block is saved Then the event returns to Planning/change review automatically, the assigned Coordinator is notified immediately, and the event is not cancelled (C-120, T-81)

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Deliberately revert a Confirmed event with a recorded reason
    • ☑ Notify the Organiser and registered Attendees on deliberate reversion
    • ☑ Flag other broken arrangements and retain the deliberate reversion action
    • ☑ Automatically enter Safety Review after all required arrangements are reconfirmed
    • ☑ Automatically return a Confirmed event to Planning and notify its Coordinator on venue loss
    • ☑ Retain earlier safety decisions in history without reusing them

    E08-S06 SCRUM-158 Sprint 3 8 pts Aaron Koh ✅ Done

    Conduct the Operational Safety Check as the Safety Officer

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Safety Officer assesses event safety factors; approval directly transitions event to Confirmed per T-107 without a second coordinator click."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: Rejection or change requests return event to Planning with mandatory comments; coordinator must adjust arrangements and resubmit.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-70 ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request). T-71 Add a Safety Review gate between Planning and Confirmed as the interim placement of C-70's Operational Safety Check T-72 Extend the role model from five roles to seven T-73 Write the Week 7 stories now against recorded defaults and amend after the customer Q&A, rather than waiting T-74 A Done story stays Done; new behaviour that touches it is a new story; an incomplete story is updated in place; a story is reopened only when one of its original criteria turns out unsatisfied O-39 O-40 O-41 O-42 O-43
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-006 Transactional outbox for notification delivery ADR-014 One file per Vercel serverless API route

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Events awaiting review listed with what the check needs

    Given events are in Safety Review When I open my queue Then each shows the event name, date and time, every confirmed venue with its capacity, layout and known restrictions, expected attendance, accessibility requirements, equipment and its placement, and the time it entered Safety Review, oldest first

    Scenario 2 — Structured review of the listed factors

    Given I open an event from the queue When I conduct the check Then I record, for each of expected attendance against capacity, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement and known venue restrictions, whether it is satisfactory, with a comment, before choosing an overall decision (assumes O-42)

    Scenario 3 — Approval confirms the event

    Given every factor is satisfactory When I approve Then the status becomes Confirmed, the Organiser and the Coordinator are notified with the confirmed details (E08-S03 Scenario 6 and E11-S01's "Event confirmed" row apply), and the activity log records my decision, my identity, the time and the completed checklist

    Scenario 4 — Requesting changes returns the event to planning

    Given one or more factors are unsatisfactory When I request changes and record which factors and why Then the status becomes Planning, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified with the items to address, the affected venue or technical arrangements are flagged for re-review, the decision is logged, and the event cannot become Confirmed until it is resubmitted (E08-S03) and approved (assumes O-41)

    Scenario 5 — Rejecting the safety arrangement does not cancel the event

    Given the safety arrangement as a whole is unacceptable When I reject it and record the reason Then the status becomes Planning with a visible "safety arrangement rejected" flag and the reason, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified, the event is not cancelled, and the Coordinator may rework and resubmit or cancel it through E10-S04 (assumes O-41)

    Scenario 6 — Reason required for reject or request changes

    Given I choose reject or request changes When I have not recorded a reason Then the decision is refused until I do

    Scenario 7 — Only a Safety Officer decides

    Given I am a Coordinator, an Event Coordinator Lead or any other role When I attempt to approve, reject or request changes on an event in Safety Review Then the action is refused and recorded in the activity log

    Scenario 8 — Events confirmed before this story are not re-reviewed

    Given an event was Confirmed before the Operational Safety Check existed When the check is introduced Then that event keeps its status, has no safety record and is not placed in Safety Review (assumes O-43)

    Scenario 9 — Status display and deactivation treat Safety Review as active

    Given an event is in Safety Review When its Organiser tracks it (E03-S05) Then "Safety Review" and the date it was reached are shown in plain language; and Given its Coordinator attempts to deactivate their account (E01-S11) Then Safety Review counts as an active-lifecycle status and deactivation is blocked (T-52)

    Scenario 10 — Every decision is auditable

    Given I approve, request changes or reject When the decision completes Then the activity log holds an entry with my identity, the action (safety check approved, changes requested or rejected), the event, the time and the checklist, immutable as E14-S02 requires

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

    • ☑ See every event awaiting its safety check with the information the listed factors need, oldest first
    • ☑ Record each factor as satisfactory or not, with a comment, before deciding
    • ☑ Approve an event, making it Confirmed with the Organiser and Coordinator notified
    • ☑ Request changes or reject with a mandatory reason, returning the event to Planning without cancelling it and flagging the affected arrangements
    • ☑ Be refused as any role other than Safety Officer
    • ☑ Confirm events already Confirmed before this story are untouched
    • ☑ Confirm the status tracker shows Safety Review and the deactivation block counts it
    • ☑ Confirm every decision is in the activity log

    Register for an event

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Attendees register for confirmed events selecting one or more sessions within attendee capacity limits (T-85); enforces 1 active registration per account per event."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: Guest registrations prohibited (C-35); registrations validate open registration window and pre-fill authenticated profile details.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-35 Attendees must sign up / register an account to register for an event (guest registration is not permitted). C-67 ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required. C-97 Individual attendees can register and view/withdraw their registration status (typically 1 registration per user account per event). C-107 Each venue booking is made for a specific date/time window (including setup/turnaround). Equipment reservations match the specific session timing/venue where required. Multiple bookings for the same venue/event across different sessions are supported. T-68 Retire T-20 and allow several venue bookings per event, each checked independently T-78 Confirm per-booking requirements, primary venue, request eligibility and hold conversion T-79 Restore Session as a child of Event for Release 1 T-85 Permit event registration with selected Sessions and enforce both Session and event capacity
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-018 Restore Sessions as first-class Event entities

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Place reserved in an open Event

    Given an Event is Confirmed, registration is open, and selected Sessions have capacity When I submit the required registration information and select one or more Sessions Then one active Event-level registration records those Sessions and I receive a confirmation with the Event and selected Session details

    Scenario 2 — One active registration per account and Event

    Given I already have an active registration for an Event When I attempt to submit another registration for that Event Then ConnectSphere tells me I am already registered and does not create a second active registration; selecting multiple Sessions remains part of the existing registration

    Scenario 3 — Missing fields identified

    Given a required registration field is empty When I submit Then registration is blocked and the missing fields are identified

    Scenario 4 — Unconfirmed Event refused

    Given an Event is not Confirmed When I attempt to register Then registration is refused

    Scenario 5 — Event and Session venue information shown

    Given a Confirmed Event has one or more confirmed venue bookings When I view registration Then the Event summary shows its primary venue and the selected Session details show their own confirmed venues; venues are not separate registrations (C-67, T-78, T-79)

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Register once for a Confirmed Event and select one or more Sessions
    • ☑ Receive one confirmation with Event and selected Session details
    • ☑ Be prevented from creating a second active registration for the same account and Event
    • ☑ Be blocked with missing required information identified
    • ☑ Be refused registration for an Event that is not Confirmed
    • ☑ See the primary Event venue and the venue for each selected Session

    Database Migration: 0001_connectsphere_schema.sql, 0024_registration_sessions.sql

    E09-S02 SCRUM-64 Sprint 4 3 pts Amareet Kaur (Scrum Master) ✅ Done

    Enforce registration capacity

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Enforces both per-session layout capacity and combined attendee capacity; over-capacity submissions route to Pending for Organiser review (T-85)."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: Parent event row locked FOR UPDATE during seat decrement to serialize concurrent registrations against race conditions.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-05 There is no automatic process; capacity adjustments and registration impacts must be handled manually when changes occur. C-58 Registration is governed by overall venue/event capacity, though VIPs may be added manually even when normal registration is full (as long as overall venue capacity is not exceeded). Expected attendance is a separate event-level planning requirement used for venue suitability and capacity evaluation. C-78 For multi-venue support, each venue is checked independently for suitability and capacity. Total attendee capacity is determined by the total layout capacity and the Event Coordinator will decide whether to confirm. C-98 Registration is enabled for attendees to register directly up to capacity, while Organisers can make final decision if exceed capacity. T-30 Bring E09-S02 into release 1 T-31 Session capacity is the lower of the Organiser limit and the booked venue capacity T-50 Manual VIP registration beyond the normal registration limit T-85 Permit event registration with selected Sessions and enforce both Session and event capacity B-11 T-98 Keep waiting lists at Event level; a full Session follows the Pending decision path
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-018 Restore Sessions as first-class Event entities

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Both capacity limits enforced

    Given a registration selects one or more Sessions When the request is within each selected Session's approved layout capacity and within the combined Event capacity Then it may be confirmed; if either limit would be exceeded it is not confirmed as an approved seat (C-78, T-85)

    Scenario 2 — Over-capacity submission remains Pending

    Given an Attendee submits a registration that would exceed a selected Session capacity or the combined Event capacity When it is received Then it is saved as Pending for the Event Organiser to approve or reject and does not count as an approved seat (C-98, T-85)

    Scenario 3 — Pending request approval rechecks both limits

    Given a registration is Pending When the Event Organiser approves it Then approval succeeds only if both the selected Session capacities and combined Event capacity remain available; otherwise it stays unapproved until capacity/arrangements change or it is rejected

    Scenario 4 — Concurrent submissions do not overbook

    Given one approved seat remains in a Session or in the combined Event capacity When two registrations are submitted at the same time Then at most one is confirmed against that remaining capacity and any other submission that exceeds capacity is Pending

    Scenario 5 — Waiting list remains event-level

    Given the combined Event capacity is full When an Attendee opens registration Then the existing Event-level waiting-list option is offered where enabled; a full selected Session follows the Pending decision path and has no separate Session-level waiting list (T-98)

    Scenario 6 — Manual addition allowed within both limits

    Given normal registration is full but both the selected Session and combined Event capacity have room When the Event Organiser manually adds an Attendee Then the registration is created as a distinguishable manual addition (C-58, T-50)

    Scenario 7 — Manual addition blocked at either limit

    Given the selected Session or combined Event capacity is already full When the Event Organiser manually adds an Attendee Then the addition is blocked and neither capacity is exceeded

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

    • ☑ Set combined Event capacity from confirmed Session layout capacities
    • ☑ Enforce both every selected Session capacity and combined Event capacity
    • ☑ Keep an Attendee over-capacity submission Pending for Organiser review without counting it as an approved seat
    • ☑ Recheck both limits when the Organiser approves a Pending registration
    • ☑ Prevent concurrent requests from exceeding either limit
    • ☑ Offer the Event-level waiting list when combined Event capacity is full; keep a full selected Session on the Pending decision path with no Session-level waiting list (T-98)
    • ☑ Allow manual VIP additions only within both limits and block them at either limit

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Organiser sets registration open/close dates and optional withdrawal deadline (C-24, C-44); setting close after start returns 428 Precondition."

    ADR-003 Enforce booking and assignment conflicts in the database ADR-018 Restore Sessions as first-class Event entities

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Before registration opens

    Given the Event-level registration opening date has not been reached When an Attendee views the Event Then registration is shown as not yet open and the opening date is stated

    Given the Event-level registration closing date has passed When an Attendee tries to register for any Session Then registration is refused

    Given I enable the waiting list for an Event When its combined Event capacity is full Then the Event-level waiting list is offered where enabled

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Set Event-level registration opening, closing, and withdrawal dates
    • ☑ Enable or disable the waiting list for the Event
    • ☑ Apply the same registration window to all selected Sessions
    • ☑ Show the opening date before registration opens
    • ☑ Refuse registration outside the Event-level window
    • ☑ Warn when the closing date is after the Event has started

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Joined a full event's list

    Given the combined Event capacity is full and its Event-level waiting list is enabled When I join the waiting list Then I am added to the Event-level list and told I will be notified when a place is released; no Session-level waiting list is created (T-98)

    Scenario 2 — Released place notified to all

    Given a place is released in an event with a waiting list When the place becomes available Then all waitlisted Attendees are notified and the place is claimed on a first-come, first-served basis

    Scenario 3 — Claimed place leaves the list

    Given I claim a released place When my registration completes Then I am removed from the waiting list

    Scenario 4 — Disabled list offers nothing

    Given the waiting list is disabled for an event When the event is full Then no waiting list is offered

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

    • ☑ Join the waiting list for a full event where the list is enabled
    • ☑ See confirmation that I have joined
    • ☑ Receive a notification when a place is released
    • ☑ Claim a released place on a first-come, first-served basis
    • ☑ Leave the waiting list
    • ☑ Confirm no waiting list is offered when the Organiser has disabled it

    Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/attendeeRegistration/capacity.ts

    Pre-conditions: A change request on "Community Meetup" (increase expected attendance to 10) is pending Coordinator approval

    Expected outcome: "Community Meetup"'s Expected Attendance is updated to 10, and organiser_a@clienta.com is notified that the change was applied Session variant: create an Event with two Sessions, a Confirmed booking and staffed Technical Support overlapping the first Session. On Change requests, choose that Session, request new dates within the Event and submit. Pending and preview keep Session/Event/arrangements unchanged. As assigned Coordinator, review the Session comparison and affected booking/crew, then approve. Only that Session changes; Event/publication details and the second Session remain intact. Affected arrangements require reconfirmation. In Safety Review, the Event returns to Planning and stays there until both venue and crew are reconfirmed, then re-enters Safety Review. Also verify Session-only title approval, stale/removed or foreign targets, stale previews, invalid dates/reference choices and rollback on failed notification. Removed targets may still be declined. Event-only fields cannot be submitted on a Session request. Record this human run separately from the automated browser/database evidence. Safety Review variant (T-103): repeat with an Event in Safety Review and a change that flags two Confirmed bookings. Preview leaves the status unchanged; applying returns the same Event to Planning and retains both bookings with reconfirmation flags. Reconfirming only the first booking leaves it in Planning and sends no new SO review request. Reconfirming the last required arrangement automatically re-enters Safety Review and sends a fresh SO notification. Repeat for an Event in its first Safety Review with no Confirmed history. Preserve previous safety decisions without reusing them; require a fresh SO decision. Safe-only and structured no-impact changes retain Safety Review. A failed final application notice rolls back the Event changes, request status, arrangement flags, lifecycle transition, audit and notices together.

    Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

    Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

    Scenario 1 — Change request recorded

    Given my Event has been approved or confirmed When I submit a change request describing what should change Then the assigned Coordinator is notified and the request is recorded against the Event

    Scenario 2 — Confirmed details shown alongside

    Given a change request is Pending When I view my Event Then the currently confirmed details are shown alongside the pending request

    Scenario 3 — Refused edit offers the form

    Given I attempt to edit a restricted field directly after approval When the edit is refused Then I am offered the change-request form pre-filled with that field

    Scenario 4 — Approved change applied

    Given the Coordinator approves my change request When it is applied Then the Event is updated and I am notified

    Scenario 5 — Declined request communicated

    Given the Coordinator declines my change request When the decision is recorded Then I am notified and the confirmed Event details remain unchanged

    Scenario 6 — Terminal Event closes pending requests as Obsolete

    Given the Event becomes Completed or Cancelled while one or more change requests are Pending When the Event reaches that terminal status Then each Pending request becomes Obsolete, the transition is recorded in history, and Obsolete is distinct from a Coordinator rejection (C-77, T-88)

    Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

    • ☑ Submit a change request against an approved or confirmed Event
    • ☑ See current confirmed details alongside a pending request
    • ☑ Reach the change-request form when a restricted direct edit is refused
    • ☑ Be notified when the Coordinator approves or declines the request
    • ☑ Confirm Pending requests become Obsolete with history when the Event becomes Completed or Cancelled

    Distinguish minor edits from arrangement-affecting changes

    SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

    "Dry-run preview (&preview=1) inside a transaction savepoint returns impact and revision fingerprint; save verifies fingerprint to prevent review races."

    Known Limitation / Boundary: Flags affected venue bookings and technical staff (T-104); returns 409 if arrangements mutated between preview and save.
    BDR Lineage:
    C-05 There is no automatic process; capacity adjustments and registration impacts must be handled manually when changes occur. T-16 Split post-approval editing rights B-05 B-11 C-67 ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required. T-68 Retire T-20 and allow several venue bookings per event, each checked independently O-27 C-107 Each venue booking is made for a specific date/time window (including setup/turnaround). Equipment reservations match the specific session timing/venue where required. Multiple bookings for the same venue/event across different sessions are supported. T-79 Restore Session as a child of Event for Release 1 T-104 A date or time change also flags Technical Support staffing for reconfirmation
    Architectural Decisions:
    ADR-015 Cookie sessions everywhere; no Supabase Auth in Release 1
