    T-93 Team Decision

    Keep hand-taken screenshots of manual runs in the repository, named by test case ID

    Team decision in the team chat on 15 October 2026, agreed by the product owner, after Le Xin asked whether manual runs need screenshots. Practice differed: some testers supplied screenshots in chat, some screenshots came from agent-driven browser runs, and some records were text only. Screenshots kept only in chats or postplans were not durable evidence. Decision: during a manual run (`run_type: manual`) the tester takes the screenshots by hand; agent or Playwright screenshots do not count as manual evidence. Each image is named after the TC_ID it shows and stored with its session record in `docs/testing/runs/evidence/<record filename without .md>/`, and the record links it. Showing the same images in the PR's postplan is recommended best practice, not required; the repository copy is the record. Applies to manual records whose frontmatter `date` is on or after `2026-10-16T00:00:00+08:00`, the day after the decision; earlier records are not retrofitted, because merged records are immutable (T-65), but every Sprint 3 Done story is re-run by its owner with screenshots before the Sprint 3 Review, as a new record; the story stays Done (T-74), and a failing re-run leads to a new user story. A Sprint 3 Done story with no manual record at all (E03-S11) gets its test cases and first manual run, with screenshots, before the review; that is a Definition of Done gap, not a re-run. Sprint 1 and 2 stories are left as they are, because their reviews have happened. The checker does not enforce it yet, so reviewers check the screenshots by hand.

    Limit E06-S03 withdrawal to Pending requests; separate Confirmed cancellation

    Product Owner Bryan's clarification, relayed by the story owner on 15 October 2026: the assigned Coordinator may withdraw a Pending venue request; it becomes Released, frees its occupancy and leaves the other bookings unchanged. Confirmed bookings cannot be withdrawn through E06-S03 or TC_E06S03_08; they require a separate cancellation flow. For that future flow, cancelling a Confirmed primary clears the primary designation and prompts the Organiser to select another Confirmed venue; there is no automatic promotion. This records a future-flow requirement, not a new cancellation implementation or a change to the existing Coordinator primary-selection permission under T-78. On 16 October 2026 the Product Owner confirmed keeping TC_E06S03_09 to _13 under E06-S03's current Sprint 3 plan and completing the remaining work, with unfinished work recorded honestly at sprint close; this is not a delivery claim.

    T-95 Team Decision

    Reuse Released and serialize withdrawal with staff decisions; notify the requested venue's staff

    E06-S04 owner agreement relayed on 15 October 2026: reuse Released, without a new status. Withdrawal locks the venue row FOR NO KEY UPDATE before locking its booking FOR UPDATE, then rechecks that it is Pending. If withdrawal wins, a competing staff decision gets 409; if a decision wins, withdrawal gets 409 and the Coordinator refreshes. Record actor, entity_type venue_booking, entity_id booking ID, event_id, field_changed status, old pending, new released and action Booking Withdrawn. The story owner confirmed notifying only the requested venue's currently assigned active Venue Staff, through in-app and transactional email-outbox persistence with withdrawal. Do not reuse booking_decided released's Coordinator-only recipient route as a staff notification. E06-S03 owns Pending withdrawal; E06-S05 retains Tentative hold release and expiry. Withdrawing a converted hold does not restore the hold or its expiry.

    Affects: E06-S03, E06-S04 concurrency/activity, E06-S05 boundary, E11-S01
    Follows / Supersedes: T-64, T-75, T-89, T-94; E06-S04 owner agreement and story-owner notification confirmation, 2026-10-15
    T-96 Team Decision

    Allow replacement retry after withdrawal, but follow the latest rejection's suggestion after rejection

    Story-owner confirmation on 15 October 2026: a Released replacement no longer prevents a fresh request from the same rejection; retain all historical rows, recheck submission rules and do not reactivate a Released row. A Rejected replacement still consumes its predecessor's suggestion: do not reuse that older rejection to repeatedly request the refused venue. If the replacement's own rejection suggests another venue, the next request references that immediately preceding rejection. There is no fixed two-attempt limit; a rejection without a suggestion ends its suggestion chain. Preserve retry-safe idempotency and one non-Released replacement per rejection. The all-status unique index in merged migration 0019 currently prevents retry after withdrawal; a new coordinated migration must exclude Released replacements only, retaining protection for Rejected and other non-Released rows. Do not edit applied migration 0019 or broaden the index to active-only statuses.

    Affects: E06-S03 replacement/withdrawal, E06-S04 suggestions, venue_bookings contract and follow-up migration
    Follows / Supersedes: T-94, T-95; E06-S04 owner identified the index consequence; story owner confirmed retry and rejection-chain rules, 2026-10-15
    T-97 Team Decision

    Accept bounded demo-account risk, approve two Sprint 3 follow-ups without reopening Done stories, and assign PO accountability for the SCRUM-75 venue-staff mapping

    On 16 October 2026 the Product Owner accepted the existing public/shared `seedCredential` risk for DEMO ONLY accounts, including the Safety Officer. No rotation or access restriction is selected. No Coordinator Lead, other account, bulk seed or reset is authorised. E14-S03 and E03-S12 are selected for Sprint 3, unestimated and not Done; their definitions and planned cases are in PR #296. E14-S03 replaces raw UTC edited date/time display with readable Singapore time in both existing Organiser and assigned Coordinator Activity-log views, without changing stored audit values, immutability or access. The deploy owner may load only an actual PO-approved mapping with pre/post records, and Ji Ning verifies delivery. This decision approves no mapping or assignment write. PR #272 is merged and its routing code is not blocked by that future setup; T-89's no-roster-screen decision remains.

    T-104 Team Decision

    A date or time change also flags Technical Support staffing for reconfirmation

    Product Owner answer on 31 October 2026, relayed by the E10-S02 story owner, to a yes/no question raised by the E08-S04 manual run (record 20261031-173321): EVT-1082 moved from 5 to 12 December, its venue booking and equipment reservation were flagged and reconfirmed, but its Technical Support staffing request kept 5 December, counted as Ready, and the event entered Safety Review. Answer: yes. A Session or Event date/time change flags each affected staffed Technical Support request for reconfirmation alongside the venue bookings and equipment reservations, lists it in the change preview and notifies the assigned Technical Support Staff. A flagged request counts as outstanding for readiness, so a previously Confirmed event cannot re-enter Safety Review until it is reconfirmed; reconfirming moves the request and its staff assignments to the new time, refused if an assigned technician is busy then. E10-S02 is In Progress, so its Scenarios 5 and 6 are updated in place (T-74) and it is re-estimated from 5 to 8 points by its owner (T-37, T-73).

    Adopt PR scope, WIP and reference-source guardrails

    Team decision on 26 October 2026 after repeated merge conflicts and review churn: new PRs are limited to 40 changed files, 1,800 additions and 1,500 deletions; at most 2 active-policy PRs per human author and 10 active-policy PRs total, with drafts included. The team-wide cap is intentionally a queue cap rather than six times the per-author allowance.     T-100 Team Decision

    PO interpretation: the first accepted hold or request claims its buffered venue slot; approval rechecks current conditions

    On 22 October 2026 the Product Owner approved this interpretation of existing customer choices C-01, C-16, C-46, C-60 and C-65; it is not a new customer quote. Pending, Confirmed and unexpired Tentative bookings are active claims, and converting a hold to a request keeps the same claim. The first successfully accepted claim reserves that venue's current buffered window; later overlapping claims are refused while it remains active. Concurrent new claims serialize so one succeeds and a losing request returns 409 without a row or effects. Approval rechecks current availability, concurrency and current buffers. Under C-109, a later buffer edit saves, retains affected bookings and flags the conflict; approval is refused while it remains. Do not silently release a claim, create a FIFO queue or let first approval win. Resolve through explicit rejection, withdrawal or replan before later approval. Keep C-67/T-68: different venues for one event do not conflict, and E06-S03's multiple-venue semantics do not change.

    Affects: E06-S06 release/product criteria, TC_E06S06_01 to _07, venue-bookings contract
    Follows / Supersedes: C-01, C-16, C-46, C-60, C-65; C-67, C-109, T-68

Once all required arrangements are ready, automatically re-enter Safety Review and notify the Safety Officer again, including when the first Safety Review was interrupted before any Confirmed history. Earlier safety decisions remain history and are not reused. This is a PO-approved interpretation of the trigger, not a new client quotation or final story acceptance.

    T-105 Team Decision

    Extend T-37 with XXL=13 for E11-S01

    Product Owner decision on 1 November 2026 on PR #398: E11-S01 / SCRUM-75 "Notify users about events they are involved in" is thirteen points, not five. T-37's S=1, M=3, L=5, XL=8 has no eleventh or thirteenth step, so 13 is added as XXL, the next value above XL on the team's 1/3/5/8 progression (the Fibonacci continuation 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13). An eleventh point was rejected because it is not a step this team has ever used. The size reflects the story owning the reusable notification capability - recipient routing across status/booking, equipment/support, effective date/time/venue change, cancellation and waiting-list flows; actor, unrelated, inactive and withdrawn filtering; deduplication; private/public content boundaries; transactional inbox/outbox and email outcomes; inbox read state; cross-workflow and database delivery verification - rather than a comparison with E10-S01, which reuses that infrastructure. This is a full-story sizing correction, not thirteen points remaining and not extra sprint credit: the original five-point commitment, the sprint ledger and already-credited work are preserved, and no retroactive velocity uplift is claimed. T-73 continues to govern in-flight work. The estimate alone does not accept the story; E11-S01's Definition of Done, implementation, delivery evidence and PO acceptance stay under SCRUM-75.

    Affects: E11-S01 / SCRUM-75, both E11 backlog views, T-37, T-73, sprint reporting
    Follows / Supersedes: PR #398; product-owner decision, 2026-11-01

    C-101 and C-131 describe the Coordinator marking the Event Confirmed after the Safety Officer approves. The canonical backlog (E08-S03 as amended for C-70, and E08-S06 Scenario 3) and the code since E08-S03 (only a Safety Officer can set Confirmed) make the approval itself set Confirmed. A separate Coordinator step would need an "approved, awaiting confirmation" state and a second screen while adding no safety check, so the team keeps one step.     Product Owner answer on 3 November 2026, relayed by the E04-S02 story owner, to a question from the E04-S02 follow-up work: after deleting down to one Session the Event kept its old details, and a later Event edit overwrote the remaining Session through the 0014 sync trigger (in testing, attendance went from 30 to 60 and its layout and requirements were lost). Answer: agreed. When deleting leaves one Session, the Event's time, expected attendance, requirements and layout update to match it.     Reaffirms C-03. No capacity figure appears in any acceptance criterion. O-17 remains open, and ADR-001 continues to cite the ~500 staff figure as the scale the modular monolith is sized against.

    C-65 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 1: Venue Setup and Turnaround Time. Customer-initiated change, not an answer to a team question.

    A: ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed.

    Settled Impact:

    **New requirement** (guide step 1): nothing was built for buffers, and the earlier exclusion is withdrawn. Reverses C-18 and C-38. E05-S05 returns to Release 1 (T-66). Setup and turnaround are per-venue attributes maintained through E05-S01; the occupancy window [start minus setup, end plus turnaround] replaces the advertised window wherever availability or conflicts are checked (E05-S03, E06-S01, E06-S03, E06-S04, E06-S05, E06-S06). Bookings that conflict under the new window are flagged, never released automatically. Open: who is shown the flagged bookings (O-20), whether a conflicting buffer change may be saved (O-21), buffers against maintenance blocks (O-22).

    C-66 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 2: Venue Becomes Unavailable After Booking. Customer-initiated change.

    A: ConnectSphere needs Venue Staff to be able to mark a venue temporarily unavailable because of maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concerns, or other operational reasons. This may occur even when future events have already been booked at the venue. When this happens, the existing event itself should not automatically be cancelled. Instead, affected bookings should be identified and the relevant Event Coordinators informed that alternative arrangements are required. The system should preserve the original event information while allowing the coordinator to search for and request a replacement venue.

    Settled Impact:

    **Correction + new requirement**: the correction is to E05-S04 Scenario 2, a team assumption that refused a block over a confirmed booking; the new requirement is the replacement-venue path. Confirms C-48 and C-61 that the event is never cancelled automatically, and goes further: a venue may be made unavailable over confirmed bookings, so E05-S04's refusal of a block over a confirmed booking is withdrawn (T-67). Affected bookings become Conflicting, the Coordinator is notified through E11-S01 and may search for and request a replacement through E06-S01 and E06-S03. E10-S05 returns to Release 1. Open: open-ended unavailability (O-23), status of a Confirmed event that loses its venue (O-24), who else is told (O-25), whether a booking is restored if the venue reopens (O-26).

    C-67 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 3: Multiple Venues for One Event. Customer-initiated change.

    A: ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required.

    Settled Impact:

    **New requirement** that also corrects a team assumption (T-20, E06-S03 Scenario 3), neither of which the customer had stated. Retires T-20 and inverts E06-S03 Scenario 3: an event may hold several venue bookings, pending or confirmed, at once. Each booking is checked on its own against that venue's availability and conflicts, including the C-65 buffers. Cancelling one booking leaves the others in place unless the Coordinator explicitly cancels them too. E08-S03's "a confirmed venue booking" becomes plural (T-68). The one-hold-per-venue-slot rule from C-60 is unaffected: it is about one venue, not one event. Open: per-booking headcount for suitability (O-27), the confirmation gate across several bookings (O-28), differing time windows (O-29), the venue shown to Attendees (O-30).

    C-68 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 4: Tentative Venue Holds Expire. Customer-initiated change.

    A: Venue Staff have explained that they sometimes temporarily hold a venue while an Event Coordinator is finalising event arrangements. These tentative holds should not reserve a venue indefinitely. Each hold must therefore have an expiry date/time. If the required action is not completed before the deadline, the hold should expire and the venue should become available for other requests. The Event Coordinator should be informed before or when the hold expires, and an expired hold should not be treated as a confirmed booking.

    Settled Impact:

    **New requirement**: expiry was explicitly not required before. Reverses the no-expiry position in C-01, C-16 and C-60 and amends T-49 (T-69). Every tentative hold in E06-S05 carries an expiry date and time; an expired hold frees the venue, is never treated as confirmed, and the Coordinator is told before or at expiry through E11-S01. Open: who sets the expiry and the default (O-31), the action that stops expiry (O-32), reminder timing (O-33), extension (O-34).

    C-69 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 5: Addition of Event Coordinator Lead Role. Customer-initiated change.

    A: ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur.

    Settled Impact:

    **New requirement** (a new role and a new workflow) that supersedes the behaviour of a Done story; E03-S01 stays Done and the queue is a new story (T-74). Adds a sixth role. Supersedes C-41 and C-55: new requests are no longer auto-assigned, so T-14 is retired and new requests go to an unassigned queue the Lead works from (E03-S08, T-70). Coordinators manage only events assigned to them, extending E01-S02 to a second role; the Lead sees every assignment and active event. Assignment and reassignment notify the affected users through E11-S01. Partially supersedes C-56: the Lead may reassign. Accounts are pre-seeded under C-57; ADR-012 one-role-per-account still holds (T-72). Open: one Lead or several (O-35), whether a Lead reassignment needs acceptance (O-36), Coordinator-initiated reassignment requests (O-37), queue visibility (O-38).

    C-70 Customer (W7) Settled

    Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 6: Operational Feasibility Check. Customer-initiated change.

    A: ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request).

    Settled Impact:

    **New requirement**. Adds a seventh role and a mandatory gate between confirmed arrangements and the event proceeding. "Preparation" is not a status in the canonical model, so T-71 records an interim placement pending O-39. The Safety Officer may approve, reject or request changes; the latter two return the event to the relevant planning stage for re-review, and the event cannot proceed until approved. The customer guarantees a response, so no timeout rule is needed. Decisions are recorded in the activity log (E14-S02, ADR-009) and notified through E11-S01. Open: stage placement (O-39), trigger (O-40), reject versus request changes (O-41), structured checklist (O-42), retroactive application (O-43).

    Q: Can there be multiple Event Organisers from the same organisation requesting for events on the system with their own respective user account, or will there be only 1 Event Organiser representing their organisation and all its event needs? If there are multiple, does the system need to track of this organisational relation and or any relations between Event Organisers in any way?

    A: For this release, Roles are individual and pre-loaded into the database. Tracking multi-user organizational hierarchies is out of scope for Release 1. The team can assume that access control is based strictly on the user's role and direct relationship to an event.

    Settled Impact:

    Release 1 does not track organisational hierarchies; accounts are preloaded and access is based on role and direct event relationship.

    C-85 Benjamin (G1) Settled

    Q: (Based on the qn above) Are Event Coordinators assigned to a fixed set of specific organisations and their Event Organiser(s) to handle? e.g. Event Coordinator A is in charge of event requests made by Event Organisers from organisation A; Event Coordinator B is in charge of event requests made by Event Organisers from organisation B

    A: The Event Coordinator Lead manually assigns or reassigns any event to any suitable Event Coordinator. There are no restriction for this release.

    Settled Impact:

    The Lead manually assigns or reassigns any event to a suitable Coordinator; assignments are not tied to specific organisations.

    C-86 Benjamin (G1) Settled

    Q: Is there a max number of events that each Event Coordinator can be assigned to?

    A: Workload limit enforcement is at the discretion of the Event Coordinator Lead during manual assignment and there are no limits to be checked by the system.

    Settled Impact:

    The Lead manages workload manually; the system enforces no assignment limit.

    C-87 Benjamin (G1) Settled

    Q: If a venue doesn't meet all of an event's requirements, should the system automatically stop the Event Coordinator from submitting a booking request for it?

    A: Based on the current process, the venue check only happens after a event request is created by the organiser. The co-ordinator need to find the right venue or reject the request once the request is allocated to him.

    Settled Impact:

    Venue suitability is checked after an event request is created and assigned; the Coordinator finds a venue or rejects the request.

    C-88 Benjamin (G1) Settled

    Q: Do Event Coordinators require the abilitiy to provide Event Organisers a reason for cancelling their event? Is it mandatory for them to do so?

    A: Yes. When approving/rejecting or making major changes/cancellations, reasons and notes should be recorded and communicated via notifications to relevant users.

    Settled Impact:

    Record and notify reasons and notes for approvals, rejections, major changes and cancellations.

    C-89 Benjamin (G1) Partial

    A: There are no rules and the relevant Venue staff based on the venue selected by the co-ordinator will carry out the approval checks. This is done manually and not decided by the system. Notification can be sent to the related venue staff once he pick up the assignment.

    Settled Impact:

    Venue Staff handling is manual and related to the selected venue; notification may go to staff once they pick up the assignment. No system routing rule was set.

Is there a point during the typical event planning process when an event coordinator is permanently fixed and cannot be reassigned?

    A: The Event Coordinator Lead can assign or reassign events whenever staff availability or responsibilities change, even after venue and technical arrangements are confirmed.

    Settled Impact:

    The Lead may assign or reassign an event at any point, including after venue and technical arrangements are confirmed.

    C-91 Jacob (G1) Settled

    Q: What is the intended difference between the Safety Officer selecting “Reject” and “Request Changes”? Does “Reject” terminate the event, or can it return to planning and be reviewed again?

    A: Rejection indicates the safety arrangement as a whole is unacceptable, while requesting changes specifies items to fix. Neither automatically terminates the event.The co-ordinator need to decide based on these feedbacks.

    Settled Impact:

    Safety rejection means the arrangement is unsuitable; a change request names specific fixes. Neither automatically ends the event.

    C-92 Jacob (G1) Settled

    Q: After an event has passed the Operational Safety Check, which changes require another safety review? For example, changes to venue, attendance, layout, equipment, or accessibility requirements.

    A: Any post-confirmation material change (date, time, attendance, venue, layout, or equipment) requires re-reviewing affected arrangements and undergoing the safety check again before re-confirmation.

    Settled Impact:

    Material post-confirmation changes require affected arrangements and the safety check to be reviewed again before reconfirmation.

    C-93 Jacob (G1) Delegated

    Q: When assigning an Event Coordinator, what makes a Coordinator “suitable”? Should the Lead consider workload, availability, event type, expertise, or is this entirely at the Lead’s discretion?

    A: It is entirely at the Event Coordinator Lead's discretion based on workload, availability, or expertise; the system does not enforce automated assignment rules.

    The Lead chooses a suitable Coordinator using workload, availability or expertise; the system enforces no automated selection rule.

    C-94 Jacob (G1) Settled

    Q: If an event requests multiple venues, can Venue Staff approve some venues and reject others, or must all venue requests be approved or rejected together?

    C-95 Jacob (G1) Settled

    C-96 Jacob (G1) Settled

    Q: When a tentative venue hold expires, what happens to the associated booking request? Does the request also expire, remain pending, or require the Coordinator to submit a new request?

    A: When the tentative hold expires, the venue becomes available for other requests. An expired hold cannot be treated as confirmed; the Coordinator must submit a new request if needed.

    An expired hold releases the venue; the Coordinator must submit a new request if needed.

    C-98 Caleb (G1) Settled

    C-100 Jerome (G1) Settled

    Q: How many Event Coordinator Leads are there?

    A: The safety check sits between Planning and Confirmed. Venue and technical arrangements are approved first, then the Safety Officer approves the check, after which the Coordinator marks the event Confirmed (enabling preparation/registration).

    The safety check sits between Planning and Confirmed; the Coordinator confirms after Safety Officer approval.

    C-102 Charles (G2) Settled

    Q: Does every event need an Operational Safety Check, or only events above certain thresholds such as expected attendance, venue size, or equipment?

    C-103 Charles (G2) Delegated

    Q: Must the safety review factors (emergency access, equipment placement, crowd movement, venue restrictions, etc.) be stored as structured data, or is a free-form assessment record acceptable?

    A: The Safety Officer reviews these factors and submits an approval/rejection decision along with explanatory comments in the system. Structured vs free-form record format is flexible for implementation by the team.

    C-107 Charles (G2) Partial

    Q: When an event uses several venues, which period governs equipment availability — the combined window of all venues, or a designated main venue? May the same venue be booked more than once for the same event (for example, separate sessions on one day)?

    Q: Is setup and turnaround time fixed per venue, or can it vary per event or booking with the venue value as the default? Who may set or override it, and do tentative holds also need setup and turnaround buffers?

    A: Each venue has configurable setup and turnaround times set by Venue Staff. These buffer periods are added around event times when checking availability, detecting conflicts, and placing holds.

    Settled Impact:

    Venue Staff set configurable venue setup and turnaround times; use them for availability, conflict and hold checks.

    C-109 Charles (G2) Settled

    Q: When a venue's setup or turnaround time is changed, should the new time apply to bookings that were already approved (with any resulting conflicts identified), or do existing bookings keep the times they were approved under while only new bookings use the new values? If the new values create conflicts, should the change still be saved with the conflicts flagged, or must it be rejected until the conflicts are resolved?

    A: Existing bookings that become problematic under new buffer rules are identified and flagged for review rather than silently removed or hard-rejected on save. The coirdinator has the final approval based on his assessment.

    C-112 Charles (G2) Partial

    A: Venue Staff manage venue availability and blocks in the catalogue. The Safety Officer approves/rejects event safety checks and records comments for the Coordinator to act on. Co-ordinator need to be informed,

    Settled Impact:

    Venue loss returns the event to planning/change review; the Coordinator consults the Organiser and can pause or adjust registration.

    Organisers provide general venue and space needs; the Coordinator selects the specific venues.

    C-116 Bryan (G1) Settled

    Q: O-20 — Who should see conflicts caused by a buffer change? A: Venue Staff see them at save, the calendar flags them, and affected Coordinators get an in-app notice. B: Venue Staff only. C: Another combination?

    A: Option A. Venue Staff see identified conflicts upon setting buffers, the calendar flags overlapping periods, and affected Coordinators receive notifications.

    Settled Impact:

    Venue Staff see buffer conflicts, the calendar flags them, and affected Coordinators receive notifications.

    C-117 Bryan (G1) Settled

    Q: O-21 — May Venue Staff save a buffer change that creates booking conflicts? A: Yes; save it and flag the conflicts. B: Block the save until conflicts are resolved.

    A: Option A. Week 7 Changes.docx explicitly states that existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified/flagged rather than silently removed or blocked.

    Settled Impact:

    Venue Staff may save buffer changes that create conflicts; the conflicts are flagged.

    C-118 Bryan (G1) Partial

    A: Buffers primarily ensure room preparation and reset between event uses and holds.

    The answer describes buffers as preparation/reset time between event uses and holds but does not explicitly say whether maintenance blocks are buffered.

    C-119 Bryan (G1) Partial

    C-120 Bryan (G1) Settled

    A: Should revert to Planning review. The event itself is preserve and not automatically cancelled. Affected Coordinators are notified to find replacement venues, reverting the status to planning/change review.

    C-121 Bryan (G1) Settled

    Settled Impact:

    C-122 Bryan (G1) Settled

    A: If the booking is still active and hasn't been replaced or cancelled, clearing unavailability resolves the conflict; if replaced, new bookings stand.

    If still active and not replaced or cancelled, clear the conflict when the venue reopens; do not restore a booking already replaced.
